# **I. Overview**

## **1\. User Requirements**

### **1.1 Actors**

| \# | Actor | Description |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 1 | System Administrator  | Manage user accounts, assign roles, monitor audit logs, and maintain the stable operation and security of the entire system. |
| 2 | Training Manager | Set up semesters, manage the official internship list, approve/reject enterprise registrations, control legal procedures, ensure internship discipline, monitor student progress and at-risk cases, send late report warnings, handle internship incidents reported by enterprises, submit final academic grades, and export grade reports. |
| 3 | Enterprise | Manage company profiles, post job vacancies, screen CVs, schedule interviews, assign internal supervisors to interns, create and manage internship training plans, review and provide feedback on weekly reports, report critical student incidents, and submit final Rubrics evaluations to the University. |
| 4 | Student | Search for internship positions, submit CVs for application, update work progress, fulfill the obligations of the internship module, and submit internal feedback on enterprise quality after the internship period. Access level is determined by current academic semester (Semester 1-4: browse only; Semester 5: apply for jobs; Semester 6: active internship; Semester 7-9: view results and submit enterprise feedback). |

### **2.4 Non-UI Functions**

| \# | Feature | System Function | Description |
| ----- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Security & Auth | **JWT Validator & Blacklist** | Intercepts API requests to verify JWT signature and expiration. Crucially, it cross-references the token's JTI against the invalidated\_tokens database table to reject tokens that were logged out, ensuring strict stateless security (BR-03). |
| 2 | Security & Auth | **Password Reset Token Generator** | An API service that generates a cryptographically secure, time-sensitive (e.g., 24-hour) unique token when a user requests a password reset. |
| 3 | Notification | **SMTP Email Dispatcher** | A background messaging service responsible for formatting and sending external emails (e.g., Account Creation credentials, Password Reset links, and Late Report Warnings). |
| 4 | Training Management | **Semester State Machine** | A database-level trigger/service that automatically freezes related application and job posting data (making it immutable) when a Training Manager updates the semester status to LOCKED (BR-14). |
| 5 | Incident & Grading | **Automated Warning Cron Job** | A scheduled batch job (running daily) that scans the weekly\_reports table against the deadline. It automatically flags students who missed reports or received consecutive REJECTED statuses, feeding data to the At-Risk Students List. |
| 6 | Student Supervision (Ent) | **Evaluation Auto-Calculation** | A backend logic function that automatically calculates the total Enterprise score based on the 4 Rubrics criteria (Attitude, Professionalism, Soft Skills, Progress) as soon as the Enterprise submits the evaluation form. |
| 7 | Incident & Grading | **PDF Generation Service** | An internal service utilizing a PDF generation library (e.g., iText) to dynamically render the Final Grade Report template, populating it with student grades before sending the file stream to the Training Manager's browser. |
| 8 | File Management | **File Sanitization & Storage Service** | An API middleware that validates uploaded CVs and Evidence files (checking for PDF/image extensions and enforcing the 5MB limit) before storing them securely in the storage bucket. |
| 9 | Student Application | **Profile Matching Engine** | A background data-processing function that cross-references a student's technical skill tags (from their profile) against the required skills of active job postings to generate a sorted "Compatibility Score" on the Job Board. |

#### **b. Table Descriptions**

| No | Table | Description |
| :---: | :---: | ----- |
| 01 | **roles** | Static authorization table for RBAC. Stores the 6 system roles: ADMIN, TRAINING\_MANAGER, ENTERPRISE, Enterprise, Training Manager, STUDENT. ***Primary key:** role\_id **Foreign keys:** —* |
| 02 | **users** | Central table for all 6 actor types. Each user has exactly one role (BR-06). Supports soft delete, account locking after 5 failed attempts (BR-01), and forced password change on first login (BR-04). ***Primary key:** user\_id **Foreign keys:** role\_id → roles.role\_id, enterprise\_id → enterprises.enterprise\_id* |
| 03 | **user\_sessions** | Active session tracking. Enforces single active session per user (BR-02) and 15-minute inactivity timeout (BR-03). ***Primary key:** session\_id **Foreign keys:** user\_id → users.user\_id* |
| 04 | **password\_reset\_tokens** | Temporary tokens for password reset workflow (UC-03, UC-04). Tokens expire after a set time and can only be used once. ***Primary key:** token\_id **Foreign keys:** user\_id → users.user\_id* |
| 05 | **audit\_logs** | Immutable system activity log (UC-12, UC-13). All actions are append-only — UPDATE and DELETE are blocked by trigger trg\_audit\_immutable (BR-07). ***Primary key:** log\_id **Foreign keys:** user\_id → users.user\_id* |
| 06 | **semesters** | Internship semester configuration (UC-14 → UC-17). Status follows a strict state machine: DRAFT → OPEN → ACTIVE → CLOSED → LOCKED (BR-13). Dates cannot be modified once ACTIVE (BR-12). LOCKED semesters are fully read-only (BR-11). ***Primary key:** semester\_id **Foreign keys:** created\_by → users.user\_id* |
| 07 | **eligible\_students** | Students eligible for OJT, imported via Excel by Training Manager (UC-20, UC-21). Requires minimum GPA ≥ 2.0 (BR-19). Status tracks student progress: ELIGIBLE → PENDING → ACCEPTED → MATCHED → OJT → CANCELLED. Records can be locked (BR-21) and frozen when semester is LOCKED (BR-14). ***Primary key:** eligible\_id **Foreign keys:** semester\_id → semesters.semester\_id, user\_id → users.user\_id, cancelled\_by → users.user\_id* |
| 08 | **system\_announcements** | System-wide announcements created by Training Manager (UC-28). Supports DRAFT, PUBLISHED, and ARCHIVED statuses. Can be linked to a specific semester. ***Primary key:** announcement\_id **Foreign keys:** semester\_id → semesters.semester\_id, created\_by → users.user\_id* |
| 09 | **enterprises** | Enterprise/company profiles (UC-30, UC-31, UC-19). Approval workflow: PENDING → APPROVED / REJECTED. Rejection reason is mandatory when rejected (BR-15). ***Primary key:** enterprise\_id **Foreign keys:** approved\_by → users.user\_id* |
| 10 | **semester\_enterprises** | Junction table: Enterprises register to participate in a specific semester (UC-18, UC-19). Each enterprise can register once per semester (UNIQUE constraint). Rejection reason is mandatory when rejected (BR-15). ***Primary key:** semester\_enterprise\_id **Foreign keys:** semester\_id → semesters.semester\_id, enterprise\_id → enterprises.enterprise\_id, reviewed\_by → users.user\_id* |
| 11 | **job\_posts** | Job postings by enterprises within a semester (UC-32, UC-33). Each post belongs to one enterprise (BR-25). Status: OPEN / CLOSED — new applications are blocked when CLOSED (BR-26). ***Primary key:** job\_post\_id **Foreign keys:** enterprise\_id → enterprises.enterprise\_id, semester\_id → semesters.semester\_id* |
| 12 | **applications** | Student applications to job posts (UC-34 → UC-36, UC-44 → UC-46). Status flow: PENDING → SCREENING\_PASSED / SCREENING\_REJECTED → INTERVIEW\_SCHEDULED → ACCEPTED / REJECTED / WITHDRAWN. One active application per student per job post (BR-35). CV snapshot is saved at submission time (BR-36). Withdrawal only before deadline (BR-37). ***Primary key:** application\_id **Foreign keys:** job\_post\_id → job\_posts.job\_post\_id, student\_id → users.user\_id, screened\_by → users.user\_id* |
| 13 | **interviews** | Interview scheduling and results (UC-37, UC-38, UC-47, UC-48). Scheduled datetime must be in the future (BR-32). Only SCREENING\_PASSED applications can have interviews (BR-33). Result (PASS/FAIL) can only be set when status \= COMPLETED (BR-34). Student confirmation is irreversible (BR-38). ***Primary key:** interview\_id **Foreign keys:** application\_id → applications.application\_id, decided\_by → users.user\_id* |
| 14 | **student\_profiles** | Student personal profiles and CV management (UC-41). One-to-one with users table (UNIQUE constraint). CV file size limited to 5MB (BR-28). PDF format only (BR-27). ***Primary key:** profile\_id **Foreign keys:** user\_id → users.user\_id (UNIQUE — 1:1)* |
| 15 | **Enterprises** | Enterprise-specific information linked to an enterprise (UC-55). One-to-one with users table (UNIQUE constraint). Each Enterprise belongs to exactly one enterprise. ***Primary key:** Enterprise\_id **Foreign keys:** user\_id → users.user\_id (UNIQUE — 1:1), enterprise\_id → enterprises.enterprise\_id* |
| 16 | **Enterprise\_assignments** | Central table linking a Enterprise to a Student for a specific semester (UC-40, UC-55). Each Enterprise-student-semester combination is unique. Status: ACTIVE / COMPLETED / TERMINATED. ***Primary key:** assignment\_id **Foreign keys:** Enterprise\_id → Enterprises.Enterprise\_id, student\_id → users.user\_id, semester\_id → semesters.semester\_id, assigned\_by → users.user\_id* |
| 17 | **internship\_plans** | Training plan header created by Enterprise for each assignment (UC-56, UC-49). One-to-one with Enterprise\_assignments (UNIQUE constraint). ***Primary key:** plan\_id **Foreign keys:** assignment\_id → Enterprise\_assignments.assignment\_id (UNIQUE — 1:1)* |
| 18 | **internship\_plan\_items** | Individual tasks/activities within a training plan (BR-42, BR-43). Each item has a week number, task description, and target date. Target date must fall within the semester date range (BR-43, enforced by trigger). ***Primary key:** plan\_item\_id **Foreign keys:** plan\_id → internship\_plans.plan\_id* |
| 19 | **Enterprise\_evaluations** | Final rubric-based evaluation by Enterprise (UC-60). Four criteria scored 0–10: Attitude (20%), Professionalism (40%), Soft Skills (20%), Progress (20%). Total score is auto-calculated using GENERATED column (BR-47). Locked after submission (BR-48). ***Primary key:** evaluation\_id **Foreign keys:** assignment\_id → Enterprise\_assignments.assignment\_id (UNIQUE — 1:1)* |
| 20 | **weekly\_reports** | Student weekly work reports (UC-50, UC-51, UC-52, UC-57). One report per week per assignment (UNIQUE constraint). Status: NOT\_SUBMITTED → SUBMITTED → APPROVED / REJECTED. Content cannot be edited once SUBMITTED or APPROVED (BR-UC52-01). ***Primary key:** report\_id **Foreign keys:** assignment\_id → Enterprise\_assignments.assignment\_id* |
| 21 | **report\_feedbacks** | Enterprise feedback on weekly reports (UC-58). Action: APPROVED or REJECTED. Feedback text is mandatory when rejecting (BR-44). ***Primary key:** feedback\_id **Foreign keys:** report\_id → weekly\_reports.report\_id, Enterprise\_id → Enterprises.Enterprise\_id* |
| 22 | **final\_reports** | Student final internship report submission (UC-53). One-to-one with Enterprise\_assignments (UNIQUE constraint). PDF format only (BR-39). Late submission is tracked (BR-40). ***Primary key:** final\_report\_id **Foreign keys:** assignment\_id → Enterprise\_assignments.assignment\_id (UNIQUE — 1:1)* |
| 23 | **Training Manager\_assignments** | Assigns a Training Manager to supervise Students during a semester (UC-61). Each Training Manager-student-semester combination is unique. Assigned by Training Manager. ***Primary key:** Training Manager\_assignment\_id **Foreign keys:** Training Manager\_id → users.user\_id, student\_id → users.user\_id, semester\_id → semesters.semester\_id, assigned\_by → users.user\_id* |
| 24 | **incidents** | Critical incident reports by Enterprise or Training Manager (UC-59, UC-64). Categories: PROLONGED\_ABSENCE, DISCIPLINARY\_VIOLATION, POOR\_ATTITUDE, CONFIDENTIALITY\_BREACH, OTHER (BR-45). Resolution note is mandatory when status \= RESOLVED (BR-50). ***Primary key:** incident\_id **Foreign keys:** assignment\_id → Enterprise\_assignments.assignment\_id, reported\_by → users.user\_id, resolved\_by → users.user\_id* |
| 25 | **Training Manager\_warnings** | Automated warnings sent to students for late weekly report submissions (UC-63, BR-49). Issued by the supervising Training Manager for a specific week. ***Primary key:** warning\_id **Foreign keys:** Training Manager\_id → users.user\_id, student\_id → users.user\_id, semester\_id → semesters.semester\_id* |
| 26 | **final\_grades** | Final university grades assigned by Training Manager (UC-65, UC-66). Grade range: 0.0–10.0 (BR-51). Overall status: PASSED / FAILED / CANCELLED. One grade per student per semester (UNIQUE constraint). Locked after submission, with audit trail for cancellations. ***Primary key:** grade\_id **Foreign keys:** student\_id → users.user\_id, Training Manager\_id → users.user\_id, semester\_id → semesters.semester\_id, cancelled\_by → users.user\_id* |
| 27 | **notifications** | In-app notification system for all actors. Types: WARNING, INCIDENT, REPORT\_FEEDBACK, INTERVIEW\_INVITE, APPLICATION\_UPDATE, GRADE\_PUBLISHED, SYSTEM\_ANNOUNCEMENT. Tracks read/unread status. ***Primary key:** notification\_id **Foreign keys:** recipient\_id → users.user\_id* |

# **II. Requirement Specifications**

## **1\. Common Functions & System Administration** 

### **1.1 UC-01\_Log into the system** 

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: |  UC-01 Log into the system  |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----- | :---- |
| Created By: |  QuangND | Date Created: | 19/May/2026  |
| Primary Actor: |  All Actors  | Secondary Actors: | None  |
| Trigger: | User accesses the Login page of the UEIMS.  |  |  |
| Description: | Allows users to authenticate their identity to access the system using their registered internal accounts.  |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: User account has been created and authorized in the system.  |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: User logs in successfully, system returns a Stateless JWT Access Token (containing User ID and mapped Permissions), and redirects to the Dashboard.  POST-2: The system tracks the successful login in the System Log.. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **1.0 Login with an internal account** 1\. User enters Email and Password into the form and clicks the "Login" button. 2\. System validates the login credentials (see 1.0.E1, 1.0.E2) and generates a secure JWT payload.  3\. System logs the action and redirects the user to the Dashboard |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | None  |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **1.0.E1 Incorrect login credentials** 1\. System displays an error message: "Invalid email or password." 2\. If failed 5 consecutive times, the system locks the account (BR-01). 3\. User is prompted to re-enter credentials. **1.0.E2 Account is deactivated** 1\. System displays an error message: "Your account has been locked. Please contact the Admin."  2\. Use case terminates. |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have   |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Very High (Every user session) |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-01, BR-02, BR-03  |  |  |
| Other Information: | Passwords must never be transmitted as plain text. Passwords are securely hashed (BCrypt) in the database |  |  |
| Assumptions: | Assume that users remember their registered email addresses.  |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

#### 

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **BR-01**  | Account Lockout | User accounts are temporarily locked for 30 minutes after 5 consecutive failed login attempts. |
| **BR-02**  | Simultaneous Session Control  | A user can only maintain one active session. Logging in from a new device invalidates the previous session. |
| **BR-03** | Token Expiration  | User session tokens automatically expire after 15 minutes of complete inactivity. |

### **1.2 UC-02\_Log out**

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: |  UC-02 Log out   |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----- | :---- |
| Created By: |  QuangND | Date Created: | 19/May/2026  |
| Primary Actor: |  All Actors  | Secondary Actors: | None  |
| Trigger: | User clicks the "Logout" button on the system header or profile menu.  |  |  |
| Description: | Destroys the user's active session by adding the JWT to the Blacklist table and redirects them back to the Login page..  |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: User is currently logged into the system.  |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The user's JWT ID (jti) is added to the invalidated\_tokens blacklist. POST-2: User is restricted from accessing internal pages without authenticating again. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **2.0 System Logout**  1\. User clicks the "Logout" button.  2\. System calls the authentication service to insert the active token JTI into the invalidated\_tokens table.  3\. System redirects the user to the Login page. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | None  |  |  |
| Exceptions: | None  |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have   |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | High (Every time a user finishes a session). |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-03 |  |  |
| Other Information: | If the token is a JWT, it is appended to the server-side token blacklist until its natural expiration time to prevent reuse.  |  |  |
| Assumptions: | None |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **BR-03** | Token Expiration  | User session tokens automatically expire after 15 minutes of complete inactivity. |

### **1.3 UC-03\_Forgot password**

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-03 Forgot password  |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----- | :---- |
| Created By: |  QuangND | Date Created: | 19/May/2026  |
| Primary Actor: |  All Actors  | Secondary Actors: | Email System (SMTP)  |
| Trigger: | User clicks the "Forgot Password?" link on the Login screen.  |  |  |
| Description: | Allows internal account users to request a password reset link via email when they forget their credentials. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | None |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: A secure, time-sensitive password reset link is generated and dispatched to the user's email. . |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **3.0 Request password reset** 1\. User enters their registered Email address and clicks the "Send Request" button. 2\. System verifies the existence of the email address in the database (see 3.0.E1). 3\. System generates a secure, unique reset Token. 4\. System dispatches an email containing the reset link embedded with the Token. 5\. System displays a success message instructing the user to check their inbox. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | None  |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **3.0.E1 Email does not exist** (Branches from step 2 of 3.0) 1\. System displays an error message: "Email address not found in the system." 2\. User is prompted to re-enter the email address (rejoins step 1 of 3.0). |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have   |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Low |  |  |
| Business Rules: | None |  |  |
| Other Information: | To mitigate user enumeration attacks, the system response time remains consistent regardless of whether the email exists. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The external SMTP server configuration is valid and operational. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

### None

### **1.4 UC-04\_Reset password** 

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-04 Reset password |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----- | :---- |
| Created By: |  QuangND | Date Created: | 19/May/2026  |
| Primary Actor: |  All Actors  | Secondary Actors: | None  |
| Trigger: | User clicks the reset link received in their email, or logs in for the first time with an Admin-issued temporary account.  |  |  |
| Description: | Enforces the user to configure a new password to restore or secure account access. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: The security token contained within the URL parameters must be valid and unexpired. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The new password is encrypted and updated in the database. POST-2: The specific reset token is permanently invalidated. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **4.0 Configure new password** 1\. User clicks the email reset link. 2\. System validates the token parameters (see 4.0.E1) and renders the Reset Password interface. 3\. User inputs a New Password, re-enters it in the Confirmation field, and clicks "Save Password". 4\. System evaluates password complexity constraints (apply BR-04) and verifies field match (see 4.0.E2). 5\. System encrypts the password data and updates the database records. 6\. System invalidates the token and redirects the user to the Login page with a success confirmation. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | None  |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **4.0.E1 Token invalid or expired** (Branches from step 2 of 4.0) 1\. System blocks access and displays an error screen: "This security link is invalid or has expired." 2\. Use case terminates. **4.0.E2 Password mismatch or complexity failure** (Branches from step 4 of 4.0) 1\. System displays a validation error message on the user interface. 2\. User is prompted to re-enter a valid password setup (rejoins step 3 of 4.0). |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Low |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-04 |  |  |
| Other Information: | Upon successful password update, all other active sessions for this specific user ID are terminated.  |  |  |
| Assumptions: | None |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-04   | Password Complexity  | Passwords must be at least 8 characters long, containing uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters. |

### **1.8 UC-08\_Create new account**

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-08 Create new account |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----- | :---- |
| Created By: |  QuangND | Date Created: | 19/May/2026  |
| Primary Actor: | System Admin  | Secondary Actors: | Email System   |
| Trigger: | Admin clicks the "Add New User" button on the Account Management interface. |  |  |
| Description: | Provisions a brand-new internal system user account by defining identities, operational scopes, and role bindings manually. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: Admin session contains authorized permission tokens to write user accounts. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: New user data is registered into the CSDL. POST-2: An automated transaction email containing random temporary access credentials is sent out to the user.  |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **8.0 Manual account provisioning**  1\. Admin invokes the initialization wizard panel.  2\. System displays empty data fields for Name, Email, Phone, and Role allocation selection.  3\. Admin completes the configuration forms and clicks the "Save" execution button.  4\. System evaluates database constraints for Email value duplication (apply BR-05) (see 8.0.E1). 5\. System securely auto-generates a temporary random password string sequence. 6\. System hashes the temporary string and persists the record into the database. 7\. System triggers the SMTP sub-system to dispatch the login info to the newly registered address. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | None  |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **8.0.E1 Constraint conflict: Duplicate email identity detected** (Branches from step 4 of 8.0) 1\. System stops data storage and flags the input field: "This email address is already bound to another profile." 2\. Admin is prompted to correct the structural data parameters (rejoins step 3 of 8.0). |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Occasional |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-05, BR-06 |  |  |
| Other Information: | Student system access provisions are explicitly handled via mass automation upload datasets (Import Excel) rather than individual manual entries. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The target user owns or controls the email account specified. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-05     | Unique Email Constraint   | The email address must be universally unique across all roles in the system. |
| BR-06     | Single Role Assignment  | An account can only possess one primary role (e.g., a student cannot simultaneously be an enterprise representative). |

### **1.10 UC-10\_Update account status** 

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: |  UC-10 Update account status   |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----- | :---- |
| Created By: |  QuangND | Date Created: | 19/May/2026  |
| Primary Actor: | System Admin  | Secondary Actors: | None  |
| Trigger: | Admin toggles the "Active/Inactive" switch matrix indicator on a user control vector.   |  |  |
| Description: | Controls account lifecycle state parameters; accounts marked as Inactive are locked out from system features. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: Admin cannot change the state properties of their own active session context block.  |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: Account execution properties are written as Active or Inactive in the database.  |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **10.0 Modify target account operational state** 1\. Admin invokes the state modifier control on a chosen profile item line. 2\. System validates structural parameters against safety rules (see 10.0.E1) and prompts a validation popup message. 3\. Admin selects "Confirm". 4\. System writes `Status = Inactive` or `Status = Active` to the database record matrix table attributes. 5\. System refreshes the listing data visualization and shows a success confirmation message. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | None  |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **10.0.E1 Execution exception: Action validation failure** (Branches from step 2 of 10.0) 1\. System blocks the execution thread and warns: "Action denied. You cannot modify your own profile status or administrative structural locks." 2\. Use case terminates. |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Occasional. |  |  |
| Business Rules: | None |  |  |
| Other Information: | Setting an active account status flag property to Inactive forces an immediate teardown of active session authentication blocks (Force Logout) on the next API call event.  |  |  |
| Assumptions: | None |  |  |

### **2.2 UC-15\_Create New Semester**

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-15 Create New Semester |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Created By: | HuanHM | Date Created: | 20/05/2026 |
| Primary Actor: | Training Manager | Secondary Actors: | None |
| Trigger: | A new OJT semester needs to be established (typically at the beginning of each academic period). |  |  |
| Description: | The Training Manager creates a new semester by defining basic information, time frame, and initial configuration to prepare for the entire OJT cycle. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: The Training Manager is logged into the system with appropriate privileges. PRE-2: No overlapping semester with the same code or conflicting timeline exists. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: new semester is successfully created with initial status “Draft”.  POST-2: The semester appears in the Semester List (UC-14). |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **15.0 Create New Semester Record**  1\. The Training Manager navigates to the “Semester Management” module.  2\. The Training Manager clicks “Create New Semester”.  3\. The System displays the creation form.  4\. The Training Manager enters: Semester Code (e.g., 2026-Summer), Semester Name, Start Date, End Date, and other configuration (optional).  5\. The System validates the data (no duplicate code, logical timeline) \[BR-03\].  6\. The Training Manager clicks “Save”.  7\. The System creates the new semester with default status “Draft”.  8\. The System displays a success message and offers to navigate to the new semester details. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **15.1 Copy Settings from Template** The Training Manager can copy settings from a previous semester (template). |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **15.0.E1 Validation Error (Duplicate Code/Invalid Timeline)**  1\. Validation Error: If Semester Code already exists or timeline is invalid (End Date ≤ Start Date, overlapping with another semester), the System highlights the error and prevents saving. **15.0.E2 Duplicate Timeline Warning**  2\. Duplicate Timeline: If the new semester timeline overlaps with an existing one, the System shows a warning. |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Low (1–2 times per year) |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-08, BR-09, BR-10 |  |  |
| Other Information: | Semester Code should follow a consistent naming convention. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | Training Manager has clear academic calendar information before creation. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-8  | Unique Semester Code. | Semester codes (e.g., SU26) must be strictly unique system-wide. |
| BR-9 | Timeline Integrity | A semester's Start Date must strictly precede its End Date. |
| BR-10 | Initial Semester Status | Newly created semesters must inherently start with the "Draft" status. |

### **2.3 UC-16\_Edit Semester Information**

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-16 Edit Semester Information |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Created By: | HuanHM | Date Created: | 20/05/2026 |
| Primary Actor: | Training Manager | Secondary Actors: | None |
| Trigger: | There is a need to adjust the information or timeline of an existing semester. |  |  |
| Description: | The Training Manager modifies basic information and timeline of a semester that has not been locked yet. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: The Training Manager is logged into the system with appropriate privileges.  PRE-2: The selected semester has not been locked (status ≠ Locked). |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: Semester information is successfully updated. POST-2: Related rules (application period, notifications…) are affected accordingly. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **16.0 Modify Existing Semester Details**  1\. The Training Manager navigates to “Semester Management” module (UC-14).  2\. The Training Manager selects the desired semester from the list.  3\. The Training Manager clicks “Edit Semester”.  4\. The System displays current semester information in editable form. 5\. The Training Manager modifies necessary fields (Name, Start Date, End Date, etc.).  6\. The System validates the changes \[BR-11, BR-12\].  7\. The Training Manager clicks “Save”.  8\. The System updates the semester information and displays a success message. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | None |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **16.0.E1 Invalid Timeline or Overlap**  Invalid Timeline: If the new timeline is invalid or overlaps with another semester, the System shows error and prevents saving. **16.0.E2 Locked Semester**  Locked Semester: If the semester is already “Locked”, the System disables the Edit function and shows a notification.  **16.0.E3 Data Conflict on Active/Approved Semester**   Data Conflict: If the semester status is “Active” or beyond, the System disables editing for core fields (Semester Code, Start Date, End Date, Eligibility Criteria) and displays a warning about potential impact.  |  |  |
| Priority: | High |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Medium |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-11, BR-12 |  |  |
| Other Information: | Changes to timeline may affect application periods and student access. Audit log should record all edits. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | Major changes to timeline should be done before the semester becomes active. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rule** 

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-11 | Locked Semester Edit Block | Semesters holding a "Locked" status are read-only and cannot be edited. |
| BR-12 | Date Modification Constraint  | Modifying dates of an "Active" semester is restricted and requires overriding confirmations..  |

### **2.4 UC-17\_Update Semester Status**

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-17 Update Semester Status |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Created By: | HuanHM | Date Created: | 20/05/2026 |
| Primary Actor: | Training Manager | Secondary Actors: | None |
| Trigger: | A change in the operational status of a semester (e.g., opening applications, closing period) is required. |  |  |
| Description: | Change the status of a semester (Close/Open/Active) to automatically prevent students from submitting applications for the wrong term. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: The Training Manager is logged into the system. PRE-2: The semester data has not been locked. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The semester status is successfully updated to the target state. The full permissible status lifecycle is: Draft → Open → Active → Closed → Locked. The system enforces this one-directional state machine and rejects any backward or invalid transitions (BR-13). Note: The Locked terminal state is exclusively triggered via UC-24 (Lock Semester Data), not through this UC. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **17.0 Change Semester Operational Status**  1\. The Training Manager navigates to the “Semester Management” module.  2\. The Training Manager selects the desired semester from the list.  3\. The Training Manager clicks "Update Status" and selects the new status (e.g., Active, Closed, Open).  4\. The System validates the status change (e.g., adherence to **BR-13 (Status State Machine)** ).  5\. The System updates the semester status and displays a success message. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **17.1 Restoring the Previous State** Rollback to Previous Status: Training Manager chooses to undo the last status change within a short time window (e.g., 5 minutes) before the change is fully applied across the system.  |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **17.0.E1 Invalid Status Transition**  Invalid Status Change: If the requested status transition is invalid (e.g., Active to Open), the System displays an error message and prevents the change. **17.0.E2 Data Lock Conflict**  Data Lock Conflict: If the requested semester is currently in the “Locked” status (via UC-24), the System prevents status update and displays a message: *“Semester data is locked. Contact System Admin to unlock.”*  |  |  |
| Priority: | High |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | High |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-13, BR-14 |  |  |
| Other Information: | 1\. Requires system validation logic for permissible status changes.  2\. State Transition Table (Governed by BR-13): Allowed transitions are: Open \-\> Active \-\> Closed \-\> Locked (UC-24).   3\. Invalid transitions (e.g., Active to Open, Closed to Draft) must be blocked by the system.  |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The available statuses (Open, Closed, Active) are clearly defined regarding their impact on user access. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-13 | Status State Machine | Semester status only transitions forward: Draft → Open → Active → Closed → Locked. |
| BR-14 | Permanent Lock Implication | Setting status to "Locked" permanently freezes all related OJT data (Read-Only). |

### **2.8 UC-21\_Import Student List via Excel**

#### **a. Functional Description**

| UC ID and Name: | UC-21 Import Eligible Students (Excel) |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Created By: | HuanHM | Date Created: | 20/05/2026 |
| Primary Actor: | Training Manager | Secondary Actors: | None |
| Trigger: | The Training Manager needs to import a large number of eligible students from the university’s academic system. |  |  |
| Description: | Upload a large list of eligible students from the university's academic system into the UEIMS system using an Excel file, helping to quickly update the list of students qualified for internship. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: The Training Manager is logged into the system. PRE-2: A valid semester is selected. PRE-3: The Excel file adheres to the required template format. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: Valid student records are added/updated in the system. Import results (success and errors) are clearly reported. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **21.0 Import Student List via Excel**  1\. The Training Manager navigates to the "Eligible OJT Student List" module. 2\. The Training Manager clicks "Import via Excel".  3\. The Training Manager selects and uploads the Excel file.  4\. The System executes \<\<include\>\> "Validate Excel Data" which specifically checks: Required fields (Student ID, Name, Major, GPA, Current Semester), Data format (GPA must be numeric, Student ID must be unique), and Semester validity.  5\. The System displays a preview of data to be imported, including the number of valid and invalid records.  6\. The Training Manager reviews and confirms the import.  7\. The System imports valid records into the database and displays a summary report. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **21.1 Only Submit Valid Documents** The Training Manager chooses to import only valid records and skips erroneous ones. |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **21.0.E1 Invalid File Format or Template**  Invalid file format or incorrect template → System rejects the file and shows detailed error. \- 5a. Many records fail validation → System highlights errors and allows the Training Manager to download the error log. **21.0.E2 Many Records Fail Validation**  Duplicate Student ID: If a Student ID in the file already exists with a status other than “Eligible” in the selected semester, the System flags the record as Invalid and uses the existing record’s data (or overwrites based on BR-18 Data Integrity Rule). \- 5c. Data Integrity Violation: If a record passes format check but violates a Business Rule (e.g., GPA \< Min required GPA), the System rejects that record and logs the specific BR violation.  |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Medium (1-2 times per semester) |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-17, BR-18, BR-19 |  |  |
| Other Information: | Excel Template Detail: Mandatory columns: Student ID (Text, Unique), Full Name (Text), Major (Text), GPA (Decimal, Min 2.0), Current Semester (Number, from 1 to 9). |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The Excel file is exported from the university’s official academic management system. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-17 | Excel Mandatory Fields | Excel imports require: Student ID (Unique), Full Name, Major, and GPA. |
| BR-18 | Duplicate ID Handling | New Excel imports overwrite existing student data ONLY IF current status is 'Eligible' or 'Pending'. |
| BR-19 | Minimum Eligibility GPA | Students must hold a GPA of 2.0 or higher to be imported into the Eligible list.  |

Advanced Search/Filter: The Training Manager applies complex filters (e.g., Major AND GPA \> 3.0, or Enterprise Status is Pending AND Registration Date \< 30 days).  2\. Pagination and Sorting: The System automatically paginates the list (e.g., 50 records per page) and allows sorting by multiple columns (e.g., Student ID ascending, GPA descending).  |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **22.0.E1 System Data Extraction Failure** 1\. The system fails to compile the list due to a connection issue or server error.  2\. The system displays an error message: "The data export process failed due to a system error. Please try again later."  3\. The use case terminates. **22.0.E2 Data Volume Threshold Exceeded** 1\. The system detects that the filtered dataset exceeds the maximum processing threshold (applies BR-20).  2\. The system blocks file generation and displays a warning: "Data export failed. The number of records exceeded the maximum threshold. Please apply a more granular filter."  3\. The use case terminates. |  |  |
| Priority: | High |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Medium |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-20 |  |  |
| Other Information: | None |  |  |
| Assumptions: | None |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-20 | Export Volume Limit    | Data exports are capped at a maximum of 10,000 records per transaction. |

### **2.10 UC-23\_Approve Official OJT List**

#### **a. Functional Description**

| UC ID and Name: |  UC-23 Approve Official OJT List |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Created By: |  HuanHM | Date Created: |  20/05/2026 |
| Primary Actor: |  Training Manager | Secondary Actors: |  None |
| Trigger: | The enterprise-student matching phase has been completed and final placement results are submitted for official approval. |  |  |
| Description: |  The Training Manager reviews the final list of matched students and enterprises, formally approves the official OJT placements, updates the students’ status to “OJT”, triggers automated notifications, and applies data lock according to business rules. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: The Training Manager is logged into the system with appropriate privileges. PRE-2: The enterprise interview and selection phase has been completed. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The approved students’ status is updated to “OJT”. POST-2: The System locks the approved records from any further modification \[BR-23\]. POST-3: Automated confirmation emails are sent to the relevant students and enterprises. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **23.0 Approve Official OJT List**  1\. The Training Manager navigates to the “Approve Official OJT List” module. 2\. The System displays a list of students who are ready for official approval. 3\. The Training Manager reviews the list (optionally using filters by Major or Enterprise), selects the desired records, and clicks the “Approve Official List” button. 4\. The System validates that all selected students hold an “Accepted” or “Matched” status \[BR-22\]. 5\. The System updates the status of the valid selected students to “OJT”. 6\. The System executes the \<\<include\>\> UC “Send Email Notification”. 7\. The System applies the Approval Data Lock on the approved records \[BR-14\]. 8\. The System displays a success message. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **23.1 Filtering, Bulk Approval, and Partial Approval** 1\. Filter and Bulk Approval: The Training Manager uses filters (by Major, by Enterprise) and bulk selection to review and approve students in specific batches. 2\. Partial Approval after Exception: The Training Manager reviews the list after validation (Exception 4a), selects only the valid records, and chooses to "Approve Valid Subset", leaving the invalid records highlighted for manual correction or subsequent action.  |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **23.0.E1 Invalid Status Violation** 1\. If the System detects any selected student without “Accepted” or “Matched” status, it aborts the approval for those records, highlights them, and displays a validation error message \[BR-02\]. **23.0.E2 Email Service Timeout** 1\. If the System fails to send notifications, the approval and data lock remain valid. The system queues the emails and alerts the Training Manager to retry later. **23.0.E3 Lock Execution Failure (Critical)** 1\. If a database error occurs while applying the Approval Lock, the entire transaction is rolled back, and a critical error is logged.  |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Once or twice per semester (at the end of the matching phase). |  |  |
| Business Rules: |  BR-21, BR-22 |  |  |
| Other Information: | Requires stable integration with the university’s SMTP server or a third-party email service provider. Proper transaction rollback mechanism must be implemented for critical steps.Security & Audit: All actions involving locking or deleting data must comply with the Audit Log (immutable records) standard. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The placement data submitted by enterprises and students is accurate and finalized before the approval process begins. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-21 | Approval Data Lock | Approving the Official OJT List automatically locks those students' placement records. |
| BR-22 | Prerequisite Status Validation | Official OJT approval is strictly limited to students with "Accepted" or "Matched" statuses. |

### **2.11 UC-24\_Lock Semester Data**

#### **a. Functional Description**

| UC ID and Name: | UC-24 Lock Semester Data (Approval Lock) |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Created By: | HuanHM | Date Created: | 20/05/2026 |
| Primary Actor: | Training Manager | Secondary Actors: | None |
| Trigger: | The official OJT list has been approved (UC-23), and the Training Manager wants to finalize the semester data, preventing further changes. |  |  |
| Description: | The Training Manager locks all internship data of the semester to prevent students and enterprises from making any further changes to groups, placements, or related information. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: The Training Manager is logged into the system.  PRE-2: The semester is in “Active” status.  PRE-3: The Official OJT List has been approved (UC-23). |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: All OJT placements in the semester are locked.  POST-2: The system records a Permanent Lock Log entry in the audit database.  POST-3: The semester status is irrevocably changed to “Locked” (except by System Admin manual override).  |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **24.0 Lock Semester Data (Approval Lock)**  1\. The Training Manager navigates to the “Semester Management” module.  2\. The Training Manager selects the desired semester.  3\. The Training Manager clicks “Lock Semester Data (Approval Lock)”.  4\. The System displays a confirmation dialog with a summary of records to be locked.  5\. The Training Manager is required to re-enter their password or a two-factor authentication code (Double Confirmation) and enters a reason (optional) before confirming the lock.  6\. The System applies the lock to all related records (BR-14 Approval Lock on Semester).  7\. The System notifies students and enterprises about the data lock.  8\. The System changes the semester status to “Locked” and displays a success message. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | None |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **24.0.E1 Authorization Failure**  1\. If the user is a Training Manager but not authorized for system-wide locks.  2\. The System displays an Access Denied message.  3\. Use case terminates.  |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Once per semester |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-14 |  |  |
| Other Information: | This action is irreversible in normal cases. Only a System Administrator can unlock in special situations. Security & Audit: All actions involving locking or deleting data must comply with the Audit Log (immutable records) standard. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | All official approvals have been completed before locking. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-14 | Permanent Lock Implication   | Setting status to "Locked" permanently freezes all related OJT data (Read-Only).  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

### **2.19. UC-32: Handle Internship Incidents**

#### **a. Functional Description**

| UC ID and Name: | UC-32: Handle Internship Incidents |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Created By: | Đỗ Minh Gia Bảo | Date Created: | 20/05/2026 |
| Primary Actor: | Training Manager | Secondary Actors: | None |
| Trigger: | Training Manager clicks on a pending incident report from the "Incident Management" screen. |  |  |
| Description: | As a Training Manager, I want to review critical incidents reported by Enterprises (or Students), document the corrective actions taken, and close the incident ticket so that issues are formally resolved and tracked by the University. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: Training Manager has successfully logged into the system. PRE-2: An incident report related to an assigned student exists and is currently in "Pending" or "Open" status. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The incident ticket's status is updated to "Closed" (or "Resolved"). POST-2: The resolution details are saved to the database. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **32.0 Handle and Close Incident** 1\. Training Manager accesses the "Incident Management" screen from the navigation menu. 2\. System displays a list of incidents related to the Training Manager's assigned students. 3\. Training Manager clicks on a specific "Pending" incident to view its details (including Incident Category, Description, and attached Evidence). 4\. Training Manager investigates the issue (usually via external communication with the Enterprise and Student). 5\. Training Manager enters the final decision and actions taken into the "Resolution Note" text area. 6\. Training Manager clicks the "Mark as Resolved" (or "Close Incident") button. 7\. System validates the input data. 8\. System updates the incident status to "Resolved" and saves the note. 9\. System displays a success message: "Incident has been resolved and closed successfully." |  |  |
| Alternative Flows:  | None |  |  |
| Exceptions:  | **32.0.E1 Missing Resolution Note** 1\. If the Training Manager clicks "Mark as Resolved" but leaves the "Resolution Note" field blank. 2\. System prevents the action and displays an error message: "Please provide a detailed resolution note before closing this incident." 3\. Training Manager types the required note and clicks the button again. |  |  |
| Priority: | Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Occasionally (Only when incidents occur) |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-26 |  |  |
| Other Information: | Closed incidents cannot be deleted; they are archived securely in the system for future auditing or legal reference by the Training Manager. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The Training Manager has already communicated offline with the involved parties to reach a conclusion before closing the ticket on the system. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **BR-26** | Incident Resolution Log | Training Managers must document the specific resolution approach before closing an incident ticket. |

Training Manager inputs or confirms the final calculated score.  4\. System saves the final grades into the database and updates the student's passing status. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows:  | None |  |  |
| Exceptions:  | **33.0.E1 Invalid Grade Input** 1\. If the Training Manager inputs a grade outside the allowed range (e.g., 11 or \-1) or inputs non-numeric characters. 2\. System prevents saving and displays an error message: "Please enter a valid numeric grade between 0.0 and 10.0." 3\. Training Manager corrects the input and clicks "Save Grade" again. |  |  |
| Priority: | Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Once per student (at the end of the semester) |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-27 |  |  |
| Other Information: | Once the grade is saved, the Training Manager cannot change it unless they request an unlock from the Training Manager. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The Training Manager reviews both the Enterprise's score and the student's weekly reports before deciding the final grade. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **BR-27** | Grade Range | Final course grades must be decimal values strictly between 0.0 and 10.0 inclusive, with up to one decimal place allowed. |

| Preconditions: |  PRE-1: User has successfully logged into the system with an active Enterprise account.  PRE-2: The target recruitment post belongs to the logged-in Enterprise and exists in the database. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The list of recruitment posts is fetched and rendered correctly. POST-2: The system updates the dashboard interface to reflect the new status immediately. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **38.0 Toggle post visibility** 1\. User clicks the visibility toggle switch (or "Close/Re-open" button) next to a specific job post. 2\. System prompts the user with a confirmation dialog (e.g., "Are you sure you want to close this job posting?"). 3\. User confirms the action by clicking "Yes/Confirm". 4\. System updates the status field of the post in the database (switching from Active to Closed, or vice-versa). 5\. System updates the user interface display to show the new status and sends a transient toast notification: "Post status updated successfully." |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **38.1 Cancel status change** (Branches from step 2 of 38.0) 1\. User clicks "Cancel" or clicks outside the confirmation modal. 2\. System closes the dialog window and reverts the UI toggle component to its original state without making any database changes. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-29 | Post Ownership | Enterprises can exclusively manage (create/edit/close) their own job postings. |
| BR-30 | Closed Post Block | Setting a job post to "Closed" instantaneously blocks any new student applications. |

### **3.7 UC-41\_ Screen Application**

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-41 Screen Application |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----- | :---- |
| Created By: | TriLVM | Date Created: | 19/May/2026  |
| Primary Actor: | Enterprises | Secondary Actors: | None |
| Trigger: | User (Enterprise) clicks on the evaluation action buttons ("Pass" or "Reject") while reviewing a candidate's application. |  |  |
| Description: | Allows users to screen round 1 applications by changing the application state to either "Pass Screening" or "Rejected". |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: User has successfully logged into the system with an active Enterprise account. PRE-2: User is on the detailed application view page (UC-35). PRE-3: The application's current status is "Pending". |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The application status is updated to either "Pass Screening" or "Rejected" in the database.  POST-2: The interface updates in real-time to display the newly assigned status. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **41.0 Screen application** 1\. User selects the decision option (clicks "Pass Screening" or "Reject") on the candidate evaluation panel. 2\. System prompts a confirmation dialog to verify the decision. 3\. User clicks "Confirm" on the dialog panel. 4\. System processes the status change, updates the application state in the database, and locks the evaluation panel. 5\. System displays a confirmation success alert: "Application status updated successfully." |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **41.1 Cancel Screen decision** (Branches from step 2 of 41.0) 1\. User clicks the "Cancel" button on the confirmation dialog. 2\. System closes the dialog screen and returns the user to the active evaluation panel without altering any system database states. |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **41.0.E1 State lock conflict** (Branches from step 4 of 41.0) 1\. System detects that the application state has already been altered by another concurrent corporate session or system automated job. 2\. System aborts the update execution block. 3\. System displays a warning message: "This application status has already been modified. Please refresh the page." 4\. Use case terminates. |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | High (Executed continuously during corporate screening cycles) |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-31, BR-33 |  |  |
| Other Information: | Transitioning an application status to "Pass Screening" makes the applicant eligible for the interview scheduling process. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | Assume that the enterprise representative evaluates candidate data fairly based on pre-established internal hiring criteria. |  |  |

 

#### **b. Business Rules** 

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-31 | CV Format Rule | All CVs must be strictly uploaded and processed in PDF format. |
| BR-33 | Applicant Evaluation Lock | An application moved to "Pass" or "Reject" cannot be reverted back to "Pending" by the enterprise. |

### **3.9 UC-43\_Manage Interview Schedules**

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-43 Manage Interview Schedules |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----- | :---- |
| Created By: | TriLVM | Date Created: | 19/May/2026  |
| Primary Actor: | Enterprises | Secondary Actors: | Email System |
| Trigger: | User (Enterprise) clicks on the scheduling management tools ("Propose Slots", "Create Interview", "Reschedule", or "Cancel") on the interview interface. |  |  |
| Description: | Allows users to handle the entire interview lifecycle, including proposing open time slots, creating new appointments, modifying times, postponing, and canceling interview sessions with candidates. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: User has successfully logged into the system with an active Enterprise account.   PRE-2: The target student has passed the initial screening phase (UC-37). |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The new or updated interview schedule parameters are successfully recorded in the database.  POST-2: The interview status state updates correctly, and a system notification is prepared for the student. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **43.0 Create New Interview Schedule** 1\. User selects a qualified candidate and clicks the "Schedule Interview" button. 2\. System displays an input form requiring fields such as Interview Date, Start/End Time, Interviewers, and Location/Online meeting link. 3\. User enters the required interview details and clicks the "Save Schedule" button. 4\. System validates the date-time formatting and checks for scheduling conflicts. 5\. System saves the appointment into the database with a "Scheduled" status. 6\. Email System automatically composes and sends a confirmation email containing the detailed schedule to the candidate's registered email address. 7\. System updates the interface and displays a success alert: "Interview scheduled successfully." |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **43.1 Propose Open Slots** (Branches from step 1 of 43.0) 1\. The system suggests available time slots. 2\. The user (enterprise) selects one of the suggestions and continues to enter the requirements. **43.2 Reschedule / Postpone Interview** (Branches from step 3 of 43.0) 1\. User selects an existing interview from the list and clicks "Reschedule". 2\. System re-opens the date-time input form populated with current data. 3\. User modifies the appointment time and clicks "Update". 4\. System updates the record in the database and changes the pointment status to "Rescheduled". 5\. Email System automatically sends a rescheduling alert email to the candidate with the updated date and time details. **43.3 Cancel Interview** (Branches from step 3 of UC-43) 1\. User clicks the "Cancel" button next to an interview session. 2\. System prompts the user to enter a reason for the cancellation.  3\. User provides the reason and confirms the action. 4\. System updates the interview status to "Canceled" in the database. 5\. Email System automatically sends a cancellation notice email along with the provided reason to the candidate. |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **43.0.E1 Past Date-Time Conflict** (Branches from step 4 of 43.0 or 43.2) 1\. System detects that the selected interview time is set in the past relative to the current server clock. 2\. System halts the save routine and highlights the invalid time picker element. 3\. System displays an error message: "Interview time cannot be scheduled in the past. Please select a future time." 4\. User is returned to adjust the time field (rejoins step 3 of 43.2). **43.0.E2 Email Dispatch Failure** (Branches from step 6 of 43.0) 1\. Email System fails to dispatch the email notification due to mail server disconnection or an invalid candidate email address. 2\. System logs the delivery failure record in the administration dashboard. 3\. System alerts the Enterprise user: "Notification email failed to send. Please contact the candidate manually." 4\. Use case terminates with the database state updated. |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | High (Executed frequently during recruitment communication phases) |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-34, BR-35, BR-36 |  |  |
| Other Information: | Any schedule modifications will also trigger immediate internal push alerts to corresponding Student's notifications center or Student's mail |  |  |
| Assumptions: | None |  |  |

 

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-34 | Interview Visibility Rules | Enterprises only see interview schedules linked to their own job posts. |
| BR-35 | Interview Time Validation | Scheduled interview times must be in the future and cannot overlap with existing appointments. |
| BR-36 | Interview Eligibility Rule | Only applicants who passed the CV screening phase are eligible for interview scheduling. |

| UC ID and Name: | UC-44 Record Interview Results |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----- | :---- |
| Created By: | TriLVM | Date Created: | 19/May/2026  |
| Primary Actor: | Enterprises | Secondary Actors: | Email System |
| Trigger: | User (Enterprise) clicks on the grading or selection status button ("Pass" / "Fail") for a student who completed their interview. |  |  |
| Description: | Records the final Pass or Fail hiring status of a student after the interview phase has concluded. |  |  |
| Preconditions: |  PRE-1: User has successfully logged into the system with an active Enterprise account.  PRE-2: The target student has passed the initial screening phase (UC-37)   PRE-3: The target student has an interview entry marked as completed in the system database. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The student's application state is permanently updated to "Passed" or "Failed" in the database.  POST-2: The system locks the application status row to prevent accidental double-grading. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **44.0 Record interview outcome** 1\. User locates the student profile within the interview evaluation grid and selects the final result option (clicks "Pass" or "Fail"). 2\. System displays a decision confirmation prompt requesting approval to log the entry. 3\. User clicks "Confirm". 4\. System updates the application state status variable inside the relational database. 5\. Email System composes and dispatches an official result notification message directly to the applicant's account. 6\. System refreshes & change the application control layout to read-only format and throws a toast: "Recruitment results saved." |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **44.1 Undo accidental selection** (Branches from step 2 of 44.0) 1\. User clicks the "Cancel" option on the modal overlay. 2\. System rolls back the active dialog box instantly, preserving the initial state without modifying data streams. |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **44.0.E1 Missing evaluation justification for rejection** (Branches from step 3 of 44.0) 1\. System detects that the user selected "Fail" but left the mandatory "Evaluation Notes / Feedback" area blank. 2\. System halts the submission process and highlights the text area field. 3\. System displays a warning message: "Justification notes when failing a candidate." 4\. User is prompted to enter feedback text before continuing. |  |  |
| Priority: | High, Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | High (Executed systematically at the tail end of interview schedules) |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-37 |  |  |
| Other Information: | Assigning a final status of "Pass" immediately updates the candidate's core index, making them eligible for Enterprise scheduling pipelines |  |  |
| Assumptions: | Assume that once an interviewer commits to a Pass or Fail classification, it implies corporate alignment. |  |  |

 

#### **b. Business Rules**

 

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-37 | Recruitment Result Rules | Final recruitment results (Pass/Fail) can only be logged after the interview session concludes. |

### **3.15. UC-49: Review and Feedback Weekly Report**

#### **a. Functional Description**

| UC ID and Name: | UC-49: Review and Feedback Weekly Report |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Created By: | Đỗ Minh Gia Bảo | Date Created: | 19/05/2026 |
| Primary Actor: | Enterprise | Secondary Actors: | None |
| Trigger: | Enterprise clicks the "Approve" or "Reject" button while viewing a student's pending weekly report. |  |  |
| Description: | As a Enterprise, I want to evaluate a student's weekly report, provide feedback, and either approve it or reject it (requesting a rework), so that the student knows if they are on the right track. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: Enterprise has successfully logged into the system. PRE-2: The student has submitted a weekly report and its status is "Pending Review". |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The weekly report's status is updated to "Approved" or "Rejected". POST-2: The feedback is saved in the database and visible to the student. |  |  |
| Normal Flow:  | **49.0 Approve Weekly Report** 1\. Enterprise views the details of a "Pending Review" weekly report. 2\. Enterprise types comments or evaluation into the "Feedback/Comments" text area (Optional). 3\. Enterprise clicks the "Approve" button. 4\. System prompts a confirmation dialog: "Are you sure you want to approve this report?". 5\. Enterprise confirms. 6\. System updates the report's status to "Approved" and saves the feedback. 7\. System commits the evaluation score to the database and notifies the Training Manager for record keeping. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows:  | **49.1 Reject Weekly Report** 1\. Enterprise views the report and identifies issues that need to be fixed. 2\. Enterprise types the reasons and instructions into the "Feedback/Comments" text area. 3\. Enterprise clicks the "Reject" button. 4\. System validates the feedback field. 5\. System updates the report's status to "Rejected" and saves the feedback. 6\. System displays a success message: "Report has been rejected. Student will be notified to resubmit." |  |  |
| Exceptions:  | **49.1.E1 Missing Mandatory Feedback on Rejection** 1\. Enterprise clicks the "Reject" button but leaves the "Feedback/Comments" field empty. 2\. System prevents the action and displays an error message: "Feedback is required when rejecting a report. Please provide a reason for the student." 3\. Enterprise enters the required feedback and clicks "Reject" again. |  |  |
| Priority: | Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Weekly |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-40 |  |  |
| Other Information: | Once a report is "Approved", the student can no longer edit it. If "Rejected", the student's Edit function is re-enabled for that specific report. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The system has an internal notification service to automatically alert the student when their report is reviewed. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **BR-40** | Mandatory Feedback on Rejection | Enterprise MUST provide written feedback when rejecting a student's weekly report. |

### **3.17 UC-51\_Submit Final Rubrics Evaluation**

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-51: Submit Final Rubrics Evaluation |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Created By: |  BaoNTG | Date Created: |  19/May/2026 |
| Primary Actor: |  Student | Secondary Actors: |  None |
| Trigger: | Student clicks the "Submit Final Report" button on the Report Management screen or Dashboard when the internship term reaches its final phase. |  |  |
| Description: | Allows students to officially compile, write, and submit their comprehensive final internship report, logged project outcomes, and upload the formal final report file for grading and validation by both the Enterprise and the Training Manager . |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: Student's internship status is active and currently assigned to an enterprise. PRE-2: Student has completed the minimum required number of weekly reports as configured by the university. PRE-3: No existing final report has been submitted or approved for this internship term.  |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: A new final internship report record is successfully created in the database with a "Pending Review" status. POST-2: The final report submission locks the student's weekly report portal from further standard modifications.  |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **51.0 Submit Final Internship Report** 1.Student accesses the Final Report Submission screen. 2.System retrieves the internship details, aggregates the total hours logged from all weekly reports, and renders the final submission form. 3.Student inputs the final internship summary, core technologies utilized, and key project outcomes achieved. 4.Student clicks the "Upload Final Report" button and selects their formal report file (strictly in PDF format). 5.System validates the file format constraints and checks that the size does not exceed 20MB. 6.Student clicks the "Submit Final Report" button. 7.System records the data into the database, locks the form from future changes, sets the status to "Pending Review", and displays a success notification: "*Final Internship Report submitted successfully\!*" |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **51.1 Student saves final report as draft** 1.On the final report submission screen, at step 6 of the normal flow, the student clicks the "Save as Draft" button instead of submit. 2.System saves the current inputs into the database with a "Draft" status, keeping the form unlocked for future edits. 3.UC stops here. |  |  |
| Exceptions:  |    **51.0.E1 Final report already submitted** 1.At step 2 of the normal flow, if the system detects an existing final report record for this student with a status of "Pending Review" or "Approved". 2.System blocks form access and displays an error message: "Action denied. You have already submitted your Final Internship Report for this term." 3.UC stops here. **51.0.E2 Invalid file format or oversized file** 1.At step 5 of the normal flow, if the uploaded final report is not a PDF file or exceeds 20MB. 2.System blocks the upload process and displays an error warning: "Invalid file. Please upload your final report strictly in PDF format under 20MB." 3.Student returns to step 4 of the normal flow.  |  |  |
| Priority: | High / Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Low (Executed exactly once per student at the end of their internship term) |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-42, BR-43, BR-44 |  |  |
| Other Information: |  None |  |  |
| Assumptions: |  The university configuration defines the exact open window timeline during which the "Submit Final Report" button becomes visible and active for students. |  |  |

 

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **BR-42**  | Rubrics All Criteria Mandatory | All 4 evaluation criteria must be scored before the enterprise can submit the final evaluation. |
| **BR-43**  | Weighted Score Formula | Final Score \= (Attitude × 0.2) \+ (Professionalism × 0.4) \+ (Soft Skills × 0.2) \+ (Progress × 0.2). |
| **BR-44**  | One-Time Evaluation Lock  | Once submitted, the enterprise's evaluation rubrics form is permanently locked. Modifications require a manual unlock request approved by the Training Manager. |

### **4.1 UC-52\_Manage Student Profile/CV**

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-52: Manage Student Profile/CV |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Created By: |  BaoNTG | Date Created: 19/May/2026 |   |
| Primary Actor: |  Student | Secondary Actors: None |   |
| Trigger: |  Student navigates to the "Profile Management" section from the system menu. |  |  |
| Description: |   Allows students to update their personal contact details, manage their technical skill tags, and upload the latest version of their CV file to the system. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: User’s identity has been authenticated. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: Student's profile data and technical skills in the database are updated.POST-2: The new CV file is successfully saved and linked to the student's profile. |  |  |
| Normal Flow:  | **52.0 Manage Student Profile/CV**  1.Student accesses the Profile Management screen. 2.System fetches and displays the student's current profile information, technical skill tags, and the existing CV file metadata. 3.Student modifies personal details (e.g., phone number, email) and adds or removes technical skill tags. 4.Student clicks the "*Upload CV*" button and selects a new PDF CV file from their local device. 5.System validates the uploaded file format and file size. 6.Student clicks the "*Save Changes*" button. 7.System updates the student's profile data and CV file in the database, then displays a success notification: "*Profile and CV updated successfully\!*"  |  |  |
| Alternative Flow: | **Flows:52.1 Student cancels the modification** 1.On the Profile Management screen, at step 3 or step 4 of the normal flow, the student clicks the "Cancel" button. 2.System discards all unsaved inputs and reverts the interface fields back to the original database state. 3.Return to step 2 of the normal flow. |  |  |
| Exceptions:  |   **52.0.E1 Invalid file format or oversized file** 1.At step 5 of the normal flow, if the system detects that the uploaded file is not in PDF format or exceeds 5MB. 2.System blocks the upload process, highlights the file input field, and displays an error message: "*Invalid file. Please upload a PDF file under 5MB.*" 3.UC stops here.    |  |  |
| Priority: | High / Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: |  Low to Medium (Updated occasionally when student details change). |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-31, BR-45  |  |  |
| Other Information: |  If the system execution fails due to network disconnection during file upload, the transaction is completely rolled back to prevent profile corruption.  |  |  |
| Assumptions: |  None |  |  |

 

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-31  | CV Format Rule | All CVs must be strictly uploaded and processed in PDF format.  |
| BR-45 | CV Size Limit | CV files cannot exceed 5MB in storage size. |

| Exceptions:   | **54.0.E1 Job posting does not exist or has been deleted** 1.At step 2 of the normal flow or during alternative flow 54.1, if the system detects that the job post ID is invalid or has been removed by the enterprise. 2.System redirects the student back to the main Job Board page (UC-53) and displays an error alert: "Error: The job posting you are looking for does not exist or has been removed." 3.UC stops here. |  |  |
| Priority: | High / Must Have  |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | High (Accessed frequently as students browse through multiple jobs to read descriptions).  |  |  |
| Business Rules: | None  |  |  |
| Other Information: | The UI should support clean formatting for rich-text representations within the Job Description section.  |  |  |
| Assumptions: |  None  |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

None

### **4.4 UC-55\_Apply for Job**  

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-55: Apply for Job |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Created By: |  BaoNTG | Date Created: |  19/May/2026 |
| Primary Actor: |  Student | Secondary Actors: |  None  |
| Trigger: |  Student clicks the "Apply Now" button on a specific Job Details screen (UC-54).  |  |  |
| Description: |  Allows students to officially apply for an internship position by submitting their profile snapshot and current CV file directly to a partner enterprise.  |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: User’s identity has been authenticated. PRE-2: Student has uploaded a valid CV file to their personal profile (UC-52). PRE-3: Student has no ACTIVE application for this specific job posting (Any previous application for this job must hold a status of "Withdrawn"). |  |  |
| Postconditions: |  POST-1: A new application record is created in the database with a "Pending" status (or an existing "Withdrawn" record is updated to "Pending"). POST-2: The student's profile information and CV file state at the exact moment of application are frozen and locked into the submission.  |  |  |
| Normal Flow:  | **55.0 Apply for Job** 1.Student accesses the details screen of an active job post. 2.Student clicks the "Apply Now" button. 3.System triggers and renders a confirmation pop-up screen displaying the name of the student's current uploaded CV. 4.System displays a critical warning alert: "Are you sure you want to apply? You can only submit your application ONCE for each job posting. No modifications are allowed after submission." 5.Student clicks the "Confirm & Submit" button on the confirmation pop-up. 6.System validates the current submission timestamp against the job post's application deadline. 7.System records the submission into the database, sets its evaluation state to "Pending", and displays a success message: "Application submitted successfully\!"  |  |  |
| Alternative Flows:  | **55.1 Student cancels the application prompt** 1.On the confirmation pop-up, at step 4 of the normal flow, the student clicks the "Cancel" or "Close" button on the modal. 2.System closes the pop-up immediately without recording any application records or modifying database flags. 3.UC stops here (Student returns to the Job Details view).  |  |  |
| Exceptions:   |   **55.0.E1 Job posting application deadline has expired** 1.At step 6 of the normal flow, if the system validates that the current system date and time have passed the deadline. 2.System aborts the transaction, rolls back database changes, locks the interface, and displays an error message: "Application failed. This job posting has reached its deadline and is closed for registration." 3.UC stops here. **55.0.E2 Duplicate application detected** 1.At step 6 of the normal flow, if the system identifies an existing application record from the same student ID for this job post ID, and its status is NOT "Withdrawn" (e.g., status is Pending, Approved, or Interview Scheduled). 2.System blocks the application process, rejects the database commit, displays a notification: "You have already applied for this position. Duplicate submissions are strictly prohibited.", and disables the submission button. 3.UC stops here. |  |  |
| Priority: | High / Must Have  |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: |  Medium (Executed whenever a student finds a matching job position during hiring waves).  |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-30, BR-46, BR-47 |  |  |
| Other Information: |  In accordance with the UI specifications, the confirmation prompt modal must follow an oval/pop-up notation over the blurred background screen. |  |  |
| Assumptions: |  None  |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-30  | Closed Post Block | Setting a job post to "Closed" instantaneously blocks any new student applications. |
| BR-46  | Single Active Application | A student can only have 1 active application submitted to a specific job post at any time. |
| BR-47  | Application Snapshot | Student profiles are snapshotted at submission; future profile edits do not alter past applications. |
