### **4.6 UC-57\_Withdraw Application** 

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-57: Withdraw Application |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Created By: |  BaoNTG | Date Created: |  19/May/2026 |
| Primary Actor: |  Student | Secondary Actors: |  None |
| Trigger: | Student clicks the "Withdraw" or "Cancel Application" button next to an eligible application record on the Application History screen (UC-56).  |  |  |
| Description: | Allows students to cancel and withdraw a previously submitted job application. Once successfully withdrawn, the student is allowed to modify their CV and resubmit if the job posting deadline has not yet expired.  |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: User’s identity has been authenticated. PRE-2: Student is currently viewing their Application History screen (UC-56). PRE-3: The target application record currently holds a "Pending" status. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The application status in the database is updated to "Withdrawn". POST-2: The enterprise can no longer view or process this specific application. POST-3: The system re-enables the "Apply Now" button for this job post for the student (allowing resubmission before deadline constraints). |  |  |
| Normal Flow:  | **57.0 Withdraw Application** 1.Student clicks the "Withdraw" button on an eligible pending application. 2.System triggers a confirmation modal asking: *"Are you sure you want to withdraw your application? You can re-apply later only if the job posting is still open."* 3.Student clicks the "Confirm Withdrawal" button. 4.System validates the current timestamp against the job post's application deadline and verifies that the company has not altered the "Pending" status. 5.System updates the application status to "Withdrawn" in the database and displays a success alert: *"Application successfully withdrawn."* |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **57.1 Student aborts the withdrawal process** 1.On the confirmation modal, at step 2 of the normal flow, the student clicks the "No, Keep It" or "Close" button. 2.System closes the prompt modal without altering any status flags in the database. 3.Return to step 1 of the normal flow. |  |  |
| Exceptions:  | **57.0.E1 Job posting deadline has expired** 1.At step 4 of the normal flow, if the current system time is greater than (\>) the job post's application deadline. 2.System rejects the cancellation request, blocks the database update, and displays an error alert: *"Withdrawal failed. The application deadline for this job posting has expired, and the candidate list is locked."* 3.UC stops here. **57.0.E2 Application status is no longer Pending** 1.At step 4 of the normal flow, if the enterprise has changed the status (e.g., to Approved or Interview Scheduled) right before the student clicks confirm. 2.System aborts the withdrawal transaction, updates the screen with the new active status, and displays an error message: *"Cannot withdraw. Your application is already being processed or has been reviewed by the enterprise."* 3.UC stops here. |  |  |
| Priority: | Must Have  |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: |  Low (Only used when students make errors or want to replace their submitted CVs)  |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-48  |  |  |
| Other Information: | "Warning: If a student withdraws their application close to the exact deadline, the system does not guarantee or extend time for re-submission."  |  |  |
| Assumptions: |  None  |  |  |

 

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-48  | Withdrawal Deadline | Students can only withdraw their CV before the job posting's defined deadline. |

### **4.8 UC-59\_Confirm/Decline Interview** 

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-59: Confirm/Decline Interview |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Created By: |  BaoNTG | Date Created: |  19/May/2026 |
| Primary Actor: |  Student | Secondary Actors: |  None |
| Trigger: | Student clicks the "Confirm Attendance" or "Accept Invitation" button inside a specific schedule slot (UC-58).  |  |  |
| Description: | As a Student, I want to officially confirm my attendance or decline an interview invitation so that the partner enterprise is notified and can manage their interview timeline accordingly.  |  |  |
| Preconditions: | POST-1: The specific interview invitation status is updated to "Confirmed" or "Declined" in the database. POST-2: The enterprise is automatically notified of the student's decision (including the refusal reason if declined). POST-3: If the invitation expires or is missed (via Exception 58.0.E1), or if the student formally declines the invitation, the system automatically updates the linked job application status (UC-55) to "Rejected" (or closes it) to fully close the application cycle. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The specific interview invitation status is updated to "Confirmed" in the database. POST-2: The enterprise is automatically notified of the student's acceptance. POST-3: If the invitation expires or is missed (via Exception 58.0.E1), the system automatically updates the linked job application status (UC-55) to "Rejected" to fully close the application cycle. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **59.0 Confirm/Decline Interview** 1.Student locates a pending interview invitation on the schedule interface. 2.Student clicks the "Confirm Attendance" button. 3.System opens a validation pop-up prompt asking: "Are you sure you want to accept this interview schedule? The company will be notified of your commitment." 4.Student clicks the "Yes, Confirm" button on the pop-up prompt. 5.System checks if the interview slot is still active and verifies the current timestamp. 6.System changes the interview record status to "Confirmed" in the database and displays a success banner: "Interview confirmed successfully\!"  |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **59.1 Student aborts the confirmation prompt** 1.On the validation pop-up prompt, at step 4 of the normal flow, the student clicks the "Cancel" or "Close" button. 2.System closes the prompt modal and leaves the interview status unchanged as "Pending Confirmation". 3.Return to step 1 of the normal flow. **59.2 Student declines the interview invitation** 1.At step 1 of the normal flow, the student clicks the "Decline Invitation" button next to the pending interview schedule slot. 2.System triggers a pop-up modal containing a mandatory text input field labeled "Reason for Refusal" and a critical warning alert: "Are you sure you want to decline this interview? This action will formally withdraw you from this application cycle." 3.Student inputs their specific reason into the text field. 4.Student clicks the "Confirm Decline" button. 5.System validates that the "Reason for Refusal" input field is not empty. 6.System changes the interview record status to "Declined", logs the text reason into the database, and displays a confirmation notification: "You have declined the interview invitation. The company has been notified." 7.System triggers an automated background update to transition the main job application status (UC-58) to "Rejected". 8.UC stops here. |  |  |
| Exceptions:  | **59.0.E1 Interview schedule has already started or expired** 1.At step 5 of the normal flow, if the current system date/time has passed the scheduled interview start time before the student clicks confirm. 2.System blocks the confirmation transaction, updates the record status to "Expired/Missed" in the database. 3.System triggers an automated background update to set the main application status (UC-58) to "Rejected". 4.System displays an error notice: "Action failed. This interview invitation has expired as the scheduled time has already passed." 5.UC stops here.**59.2.E1 Reason for refusal is left blank (Ref: BR-40)**  1.At step 5 of the alternative flow 59.2, if the system detects that the student left the "Reason for Refusal" field empty or filled with only whitespace. 2.System blocks the submission, highlights the input box in red, and displays an error message: "Action denied. You must provide a valid reason for declining the interview invitation." 3.Student returns to step 3 of alternative flow 59.2.  |  |  |
| Priority: | Must Have  |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Medium (Executed once per valid interview invitation)  |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-49 |  |  |
| Other Information: |  None  |  |  |
| Assumptions: | Upon successful interview completion and official acceptance by the enterprise, an authorized administrator or the system's background workflow will transition the student profile into an "Active Intern" state, linking them directly to their assigned Enterprise ID to unlock subsequent internship features (UC-61).  |  |  |

 

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **BR-49**  | Attendance Irreversibility  | Once an interview attendance is confirmed or formally declined by a student, they cannot undo, modify, or reverse the status via the student UI.  |

### **4.9 UC-60\_Submit Feedback for Enterprise** 

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-60: Submit Feedback for Enterprise |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Created By: |  BaoNTG | Date Created: |  19/May/2026 |
| Primary Actor: |  Student | Secondary Actors: |  None |
| Trigger: | Student clicks the "Submit Enterprise Feedback" option from the navigation menu or from a system prompt after the internship concludes.  |  |  |
| Description: | Allows students to submit a post-internship evaluation form rating the enterprise on training quality, supervisor support, and work environment. The feedback is internal and visible only to the Training Manager, enabling the university to assess and improve future enterprise partnerships. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: Student has successfully logged into the system.  PRE-2: Student's internship status is "Completed" or in the final evaluation phase.  PRE-3: Student has not already submitted feedback for this enterprise (BR-53). |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: A new feedback record is created in the database linked to the student and enterprise. POST-2: The Training Manager can view the submitted feedback via UC-30. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **60.0 Submit Feedback for Enterprise** 1\. Student clicks on the "Enterprise Feedback" option from the menu.  2\. System verifies that the student's internship has concluded and that no prior feedback exists.  3\. System displays the feedback form with rating categories: Training Quality (1-5 stars), Supervisor Support (1-5 stars), Work Environment (1-5 stars), and an Overall Rating (1-5 stars), plus a "Written Comments" text area.  4\. Student selects ratings for each category.  5\. Student enters optional written comments in the text area.  6\. Student clicks the "Submit Feedback" button.  7\. System validates that all mandatory rating fields have been completed and values are valid integers between 1-5 (BR-55).  8\. System saves the feedback to the database and displays a success message: "Thank you\! Your feedback has been submitted successfully." |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | None |  |  |
| Exceptions:  | **60.0.E1 Feedback already submitted (Branches from step 2\)**  1\. System blocks access and displays a message: "You have already submitted feedback for this enterprise. You can only submit once per semester."  2\. Use case terminates.  **60.0.E2 Missing mandatory ratings (Branches from step 7\)**  1\. System highlights the missing rating fields in red.  2\. Student is prompted to complete all required ratings (rejoins step 4\) |  |  |
| Priority: | Medium, Should Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Low (Once per student at the end of the semester) |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-28 (Feedback Confidentiality), BR-53 (Single Feedback Per Semester), BR-55 (Feedback Rating Scale) |  |  |
| Other Information: | Student identity is recorded but completely hidden from the Enterprise accounts to encourage honest and constructive feedback |  |  |
| Assumptions: | Student provides objective and truthful feedback based on their actual real-world experience at the enterprise. |  |  |

#### **b. Business Rules:**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-28 | Feedback Confidentiality | Student enterprise feedback is strictly internal. Only the Training Manager role can access feedback data. Enterprise accounts have no API or UI access to read this data. |
| BR-53 | Single Feedback Per Semester | A student can only submit one feedback entry per enterprise per semester. Duplicate submissions are blocked by the system. |
| BR-55 | Feedback Rating Scale | Enterprise feedback scores must be integer values between 1 and 5 inclusive for each evaluation criterion (Training Quality, Supervisor Support, Work Environment, Overall).  |

| Preconditions: | PRE-1: Student is viewing their report list (UC-62) PRE-2: The targeted report record must hold either a "Draft" status or a "Rejected" status. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The modified content is updated in the database.  POST-2: If re-submitted, the status changes back to "Pending Review". |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **64.0 Edit Weekly Report** 1.Student selects an eligible "Draft" or "Rejected" report and clicks "Edit". 2.System loads the previously saved report text and file metadata into the input form. 3.Student modifies the description text or removes/replaces the attached file. 4.System validates file constraints if a new file is uploaded. 5.Student clicks the "Resubmit Report" (or "Save Changes") button. 6.System updates the record in the database, updates status to "Pending Review", and displays a success notification. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | None  |  |  |
| Exceptions:  |  **64.0.E1 Status changed externally** 1.At step 5 of the normal flow, if the Enterprise changed the report status right before the student clicks submit. 2.System aborts the commit and displays an error message: "Action failed. The report status has changed and can no longer be edited." 3.UC stops here. |  |  |
| Priority: | Must Have  |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Medium (Used when reports need correction based on Enterprise feedback)  |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-56 |  |  |
| Other Information: |  None |  |  |
| Assumptions: |  None  |  |  |

 

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **BR-56** | Weekly Report Submission Window   | Students are only permitted to submit a weekly report during its designated "Active" week. Retroactive (past) and advance (future) submissions are strictly blocked. Late submissions are only accepted via explicit Training Manager override. |

### **4.14 UC-65\_Submit Final Internship Report**

#### **a. Functional Description** 

| UC ID and Name: | UC-65: Submit Final Internship Report |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Created By: |  BaoNTG | Date Created: |  19/May/2026 |
| Primary Actor: |  Student | Secondary Actors: |  None |
| Trigger: | Student clicks the "Submit Final Report" button on the Report Management screen or Dashboard when the internship term reaches its final phase. |  |  |
| Description: | Allows students to officially compile, write, and submit their comprehensive final internship report, logged project outcomes, and upload the formal final report file for grading and validation by both the Enterprise and the Training Manager.  |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: Student's internship status is active and currently assigned to an enterprise.  PRE-2: Student has completed the minimum required number of weekly reports as configured by the university.  PRE-3: No existing final report has been submitted or approved for this internship term. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: A new final internship report record is successfully created in the database with a "Pending Review" status.  POST-2: The final report submission locks the student's weekly report portal from further standard modifications.  |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | **65.0 Submit Final Internship Report** 1.Student accesses the Final Report Submission screen. 2.System retrieves the internship details, aggregates the total hours logged from all weekly reports, and renders the final submission form. 3.Student inputs the final internship summary, core technologies utilized, and key project outcomes achieved. 4.Student clicks the "Upload Final Report" button and selects their formal report file (strictly in PDF format). 5.System validates the file format constraints and checks that the size does not exceed 20MB. 6.Student clicks the "Submit Final Report" button. 7.System records the data into the database, locks the form from future changes, sets the status to "Pending Review", and displays a success notification: "Final Internship Report submitted successfully\!"   |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **65.1 Student saves final report as draft** 1.On the final report submission screen, at step 6 of the normal flow, the student clicks the "Save as Draft" button instead of submit. 2.System saves the current inputs into the database with a "Draft" status, keeping the form unlocked for future edits. 3.UC stops here.   |  |  |
| Exceptions:  | **65.0.E1 Final report already submitted** 1.At step 2 of the normal flow, if the system detects an existing final report record for this student with a status of "Pending Review" or "Approved". 2.System blocks form access and displays an error message: "Action denied. You have already submitted your Final Internship Report for this term." 3.UC stops here. **65.0.E2 Invalid file format or oversized file** 1.At step 5 of the normal flow, if the uploaded final report is not a PDF file or exceeds 20MB. 2.System blocks the upload process and displays an error warning: "Invalid file. Please upload your final report strictly in PDF format under 20MB." 3.Student returns to step 4 of the normal flow.  |  |  |
| Priority: | High / Must Have |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Low (Executed exactly once per student at the end of their internship term)  |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-50, BR-51,BR-45 |  |  |
| Other Information: | The user interface should support clear visual data representations, such as progress bars or spider charts, for different skill evaluation metrics. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | The university configuration defines the exact open window timeline during which the "Submit Final Report" button becomes visible and active for students.  |  |  |

 

#### **b. Business Rules**

| ID | Business Rule | Business Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-50  | Final Report Format  | The final internship report must be strictly submitted in **PDF format**.  |
| BR-51 | Absolute Hard Deadline  | The server rejects any final report submissions received after the exact minute of the deadline configured in the system roadmap.  |
| BR-45 | File Size Limit  | Final report files must not exceed 20MB in storage size.  |

#### **a. Login Screen**

 This screen allows user to be authenticated to the system screens/functionalities.

##### **UI Design** 

*![][image18]*

| Field Name | Field Type | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Email\*** | Text Box | This is for user to input valid email address for logging in |
| **Password\*** | Password Box | This is for user to input password for logging in |
| **Remember Me** | Checkbox | User checks to save the login session persistently |
| **Forgot password ?** | Hyperlink | User clicks to redirect to the password recovery page |
| **Login** | Button | User clicks to authenticate him/herself into the system |

##### **Database Access**

| Table | CRUD | Description |
| :---- | ----- | :---- |
| **users** | R | Verify Email & Password information |
| **roles** | R | Specify the authorizations of the logged-in user |
| **user\_sessions** | C | Record the active login session |

##### **SQL Commands:**

1/ Verify Email & Password information  
SELECT user\_id, full\_name, email, role\_id, status   
FROM users   
WHERE email \= ? AND status \= 'ACTIVE';

 2/ Specify the authorizations of the logged-in user  
SELECT role\_name   
FROM roles   
WHERE role\_id \= ?;

 3/ Record active session  
INSERT INTO user\_sessions (user\_id, token\_hash, device\_info, ip\_address, expires\_at)   
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?);

#### **a. User Accounts Screen**

This screen allows the admin to view, search, filter, and manage all user accounts in the system.

* **Related use cases**: UC-06\_View user account list, UC-07\_View user account details, UC-10\_Ban user account

#### 

##### **UI Design** 

*![][image19]*

| Field Name | Field Type | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *Search Fields* |  |  |
| Username | Text Box | Allow to search using the name or email |
| Role | Combo Box | Allow to filter the list by assigned role. Default: All |
| Status | Combo Box | Allow to filter the list by status. Default: All |
| \+Add New User | Button | Click to open the Pop-up to create a new user |
| *Data Table* |  |  |
| ID | Integer | Auto-increased identifier of the user account |
| Full Name | Text | Full name of the user |
| Email | Text | Email address of the user |
| Role | Text | Assigned role of the user |
| Status | Text | Current status of the user (Active/Inactive/Locked) |
| *Data Actions* |  |  |
| View | icon | Click to open the User Details page for viewing the relevant account |
| Edit | icon | Click to open the User Details page for updating the relevant account |
| Protect / Unban | icon | Shown when the data status is inactive or locked. This is to activate the relevant account |
| Ban | icon | Shown when the data status is active. This is to deactivate the relevant account |

##### **Database Access**

| Table | CRUD | Description |
| :---- | ----- | :---- |
| **users, roles** | R, U | Query the list of current users from the database with filters Update status of a specific user to ACTIVE/INACTIVE/LOCKED |

##### **SQL Commands:**

1/ Query the list of current users from the database   
SELECT u.user\_id, u.full\_name, u.email, r.role\_name, u.status   
FROM users u   
JOIN roles r ON u.role\_id \= r.role\_id   
WHERE (u.full\_name ILIKE ? OR u.email ILIKE ?)   
  AND (u.role\_id \= ? OR ? IS NULL)   
  AND (u.status \= ? OR ? IS NULL)   
ORDER BY u.created\_at DESC   
LIMIT ? OFFSET ?;

 2/ Update status of a specific user (Ban / Unban / Lock)   
UPDATE users   
SET status \= ?, updated\_at \= CURRENT\_TIMESTAMP   
WHERE user\_id \= ?;

### **1.3 System Auditing** 

#### **a. System Logs Screen**

This screen displays the immutable system activity log for tracking user actions.

* **Related use cases**: UC-11\_View System Logs, UC-12\_Export System Logs

##### **UI Design** 

*![][image21]*

| Field Name | Field Type | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *Search Fields* |  |  |
| **Username** | Text Box | Allow to search logs by the actor's name |
| **Date** | Date Picker | Allow to filter logs by a specific date. Default: All |
| **Export to Excel** | Button | Click to export the current log data to an Excel file |
| *Data Table* |  |  |
| **ID** | Integer | Auto-increased identifier of the log log entry |
| **Time** | DateTime | The exact time the action was performed |
| **User** | Text | The name of the user who performed the action |
| **Action** | Text | The type of action performed |
| **Details** | Text | Detailed description of the action and entity affected |
| **IP Address** | Text | The IP address of the user |

##### **Database Access**

| Table | CRUD | Description |
| :---- | ----- | :---- |
| **audit\_logs, users** | R | Query the list of system logs with pagination Query all matching system logs for Export |

##### **SQL Commands:**

1/ Query the list of system logs from the database (with pagination)  
SELECT   
    l.log\_id,   
    l.timestamp as Time,   
    u.full\_name as User,   
    l.action as Action,   
    CONCAT(l.target\_entity, ' \- ', l.new\_value) as Details,   
    l.ip\_address as IP\_Address   
FROM audit\_logs l   
LEFT JOIN users u ON l.user\_id \= u.user\_id   
WHERE (u.full\_name ILIKE ?)   
  AND (DATE(l.timestamp) \= ? OR ? IS NULL)   
ORDER BY l.timestamp DESC   
LIMIT ? OFFSET ?;

2/ Query all logs for Export function (without pagination)  
SELECT   
    l.log\_id,   
    l.timestamp as Time,   
    u.full\_name as User,   
    l.action as Action,   
    CONCAT(l.target\_entity, ' \- ', l.new\_value) as Details,   
    l.ip\_address as IP\_Address   
FROM audit\_logs l   
LEFT JOIN users u ON l.user\_id \= u.user\_id   
WHERE (u.full\_name ILIKE ?)   
  AND (DATE(l.timestamp) \= ? OR ? IS NULL)   
ORDER BY l.timestamp DESC;

##### **Database Access**

*\[Provide the design description for the screen/function to access the database here: what table the screen/function would access, which transactions does it make (C-Create, R-Read, U-Update, or D-Delete), and how/purpose of the access (by providing Description and SQL commands)\]*

| Table | CRUD | Description |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |
| users  | R  | Retrieve the logged-in student's basic profile details (Full name and avatar/image URL).  |
| applications | R   |  Count the total number of job application rows submitted by this student, as well as calculation metrics for the Application Status Rate chart.  |
| interviews  | R  | Fetch and list upcoming interview arrangements (Company name, type, date, role) for the "Up Next" grid.  |
| weekly\_reports  | R  | Query all submitted progress records to calculate the completed report ratio and compute total accumulated hours (`hours_logged`).  |

   
***SQL Commands***  
*\[Provide the detailed SQL (select, insert, update...) which are used in implementing the screen/function\]*  
 **1/ Retrieve student profile details**   
SELECT   
    u.user\_id,   
    u.full\_name,   
    u.email,   
    u.image\_url  
FROM users u  
JOIN roles r ON u.role\_id \= r.role\_id  
WHERE u.user\_id \= ?   
  AND r.role\_name \= 'Student';  
**2/ Count total submitted applications**   
SELECT COUNT(application\_id) AS total\_applications   
FROM applications   
WHERE student\_id \= ?;  
**3/ Fetch status breakdown for Donut Chart (Application status rate)**   
SELECT   
    application\_status,  
    COUNT(application\_id) AS status\_count,  
    ROUND(COUNT(application\_id) \* 100.0 / SUM(COUNT(application\_id)) OVER(), 2\) AS status\_percentage  
FROM applications  
WHERE student\_id \= ?  
GROUP BY application\_status;  
**4/ Count total interview schedules**   
SELECT COUNT(i.interview\_id) AS total\_interviews  
FROM interviews i  
JOIN applications a ON i.application\_id \= a.application\_id  
WHERE a.student\_id \= ?;  
**5/ Fetch upcoming interview details for the "Up Next" data table**   
SELECT   
    e.company\_name,  
    i.interview\_type AS type,  
    i.scheduled\_date AS date,  
    j.title AS job\_position  
FROM interviews i  
JOIN applications a ON i.application\_id \= a.application\_id  
JOIN job\_posts j ON a.job\_post\_id \= j.job\_post\_id  
JOIN enterprises e ON j.enterprise\_id \= e.enterprise\_id  
WHERE a.student\_id \= ?   
  AND i.scheduled\_date \>= CURRENT\_DATE  
ORDER BY i.scheduled\_date ASC;  
**6/ Calculate accumulated logged hours and report submission ratios**   
SELECT   
    COUNT(w.report\_id) AS submitted\_reports\_count,  
    COALESCE(SUM(w.hours\_logged), 0\) AS total\_hours\_logged  
FROM weekly\_reports w  
JOIN Enterprise\_assignments ma ON w.assignment\_id \= ma.assignment\_id  
WHERE ma.student\_id \= ?;

# **IV. Appendix**

## **1\. Assumptions**

**1.1. Organizational & Business Assumptions:**

- A1. **Formal University-Enterprise Partnerships:** It is assumed that the University has established formal, legally binding partnership agreements (MOU/MOA) with all participating Enterprises before they are registered and approved on the system by the Training Manager. The system does not verify or manage these legal agreements; it only tracks the digital approval status.  
- A2. **User Computer Literacy & Internet Access:** It is assumed that all 4 types of system users (System Admin, Training Manager, Enterprise representative, and Student) possess at minimum basic computer literacy skills — including the ability to navigate web browsers, fill out online forms, upload/download files, and manage email accounts. All users are also assumed to have stable and reliable internet access during their usage sessions.  
- A3. **Enterprise Commitment to Intern Development:** It is assumed that approved Enterprises will genuinely commit to providing meaningful, real-world projects and professional tasks for the interns throughout the entire duration of the internship semester. The system cannot enforce or verify the quality of the actual work assigned to students at the enterprise premises.  
- A4. **Truthfulness of Student Data:** It is assumed that all information provided by Students in their profiles, uploaded CVs, weekly reports, and final internship reports is truthful, accurate, and represents their own original work. The system does not incorporate plagiarism detection or identity verification mechanisms.  
- A5. **Timely Enterprise Engagement:** It is assumed that Enterprise representatives will log into the system at regular intervals (at minimum weekly) to review student weekly reports, provide feedback, update interview results, and complete the final Rubrics evaluation before the semester deadline. The system provides notification reminders but cannot force user engagement.  
- A6. **Timely Training Manager Engagement:** It is assumed that the Training Manager will actively monitor the system dashboard, process pending enterprise registrations, review at-risk student alerts, handle incident reports, and submit final academic grades within the timeframes defined by the academic calendar. Delays in TM actions may cascade into delayed student grade finalization.

**1.2. Technical Assumptions:**

- A7. **Standardized Evaluation Criteria:** It is assumed that the University's grading scale (0.0 to 10.0) and the 4-criteria Rubrics framework (Attitude 20%, Professionalism 40%, Soft Skills 20%, Progress 20%) are officially standardized by the University's Academic Board and will remain unchanged during the lifetime of an active semester. Any mid-semester changes to the grading formula would require a system update.  
- A8. **Prompt Interview Result Updates:** It is assumed that Enterprise representatives will promptly update the Pass/Fail interview outcome on the system (UC-40) within 3 business days after conducting interviews. Delayed updates may block subsequent workflow steps (e.g., supervisor assignment, training plan creation).  
- A9. **Accurate Semester Data from University:** It is assumed that the academic semester information (semester number 1-9) assigned to each student in the university's core database is accurate and up-to-date at the time of Excel import (UC-20). Incorrect semester data would result in students receiving wrong permission levels on the platform.  
- A10. **Honest Student Feedback:** It is assumed that Students will provide honest and constructive feedback when evaluating their host Enterprise (UC-50). Since feedback is non-anonymous (the student's identity is recorded), it is assumed that students will not be pressured or intimidated by Enterprises regarding their feedback submissions. The confidentiality of feedback data (visible only to Training Manager) is designed to mitigate this risk.

## **2\. Dependencies**

**2.1. Infrastructure Dependencies:**

- D1. **Cloud Hosting Infrastructure:** The system's availability, performance, and uptime depend entirely on the reliability of the chosen cloud hosting provider (e.g., AWS EC2/RDS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, or University-managed on-premise servers). The system requires a minimum guaranteed uptime of 99.5% during active semester periods to ensure uninterrupted access for all 4 user roles.  
- D2. **Relational Database Management System (RDBMS):** The system depends on PostgreSQL (version 14 or higher) as the primary persistent data store. All business-critical data — including user accounts, semester configurations, applications, weekly reports, evaluations, and feedback — is stored in this database. Database backup and disaster recovery procedures must be established by the infrastructure team.

**2.2. External Service Dependencies:**

- D3. **Email/SMTP Delivery Service:** The system relies on a third-party email delivery service (e.g., SendGrid, AWS SES, or a University-managed SMTP server) for dispatching critical system communications, including: account creation credentials, password reset links, interview schedule notifications, late report warning alerts, and incident report notifications. If the email service is down, users will not receive time-sensitive notifications.  
- D4. **External Video Conferencing Platforms:** For the interview scheduling module (UC-39), the system stores and displays external meeting links (Google Meet, Zoom, Microsoft Teams) but does not host or manage the actual video call infrastructure. The availability and functionality of these platforms are outside the system's control.  
- D5. **PDF Generation Libraries:** The system depends on stable, well-maintained third-party libraries (e.g., iText for Java/Spring Boot, or PDFKit/Puppeteer for Node.js) to accurately generate and format downloadable PDF documents for: Final Grade Reports (UC-66), student CV downloads, and final internship report exports. Library version updates or deprecations may require code adjustments.

**2.3. Data Source Dependencies:**

- D6. **Core University Academic Database:** The initial student onboarding process depends on the University's core academic system to provide an accurate, verified Excel file containing the baseline data of eligible students, including: Student ID, Full Name, Major, GPA, and Current Semester (1-9). The UEIMS does not independently verify this data against the university's records after import.  
- D7. **Predefined Excel Import Template:** The bulk import feature (UC-20) strictly depends on the Training Manager uploading student data using a predefined, version-controlled Excel template (.xlsx). Deviations from the template structure (e.g., missing columns, incorrect data types, extra sheets) will cause the import parser to reject the file and display specific validation error messages.

**2.4. Data Source Dependencies:**

- D8. **Internal Authentication & Authorization Framework:** Since third-party Single Sign-On (SSO) providers are excluded from the current project scope, the system relies entirely on its own internal security stack for user authentication and role-based authorization. This includes: JWT (JSON Web Token) for session management, BCrypt algorithm for one-way password hashing, and a custom RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) middleware that enforces permissions for all 4 roles (Admin, Training Manager, Enterprise, Student).

## **3\. Limitations**

**3.1. Performance & Storage Limitations:**

- L1. **File Upload Size Restriction:** To optimize server storage costs and prevent abuse, all file uploads across the system (student CV PDFs, incident evidence screenshots, final internship report PDFs) are strictly limited to a maximum of 5MB per individual file. Files exceeding this limit will be rejected at the API level with a clear error message.  
- L2. **Data Export Volume Cap:** To prevent server memory overload during large data extraction operations, all export-to-Excel and export-to-PDF functions are capped at a maximum of 10,000 records per single export transaction. If the dataset exceeds this threshold, the user must apply filters to reduce the record count before exporting.  
- L3. **Concurrent User Capacity:** The system is designed and load-tested to support up to 500 concurrent active sessions under normal operating conditions. Performance degradation (slower response times, increased latency) may occur during peak usage periods if concurrent sessions significantly exceed this threshold.

**3.2. Feature & Functionality Limitations:**

- L4. **No Real-Time Messaging or Chat:** The system does not include an integrated, real-time chat or instant messaging module (comparable to Slack, Microsoft Teams, or Facebook Messenger). All communication between users is strictly asynchronous and channeled through formal text areas within the system (e.g., report feedback fields, incident description areas, announcement posts).  
- L5. **No Native Video Interview Hosting:** The system does not host, record, or manage native video or audio calls for enterprise recruitment interviews. The interview scheduling module (UC-39) only stores metadata — specifically the scheduled date/time and an external meeting link (e.g., a Zoom or Google Meet URL). The actual interview execution occurs entirely outside the UEIMS platform.  
- L6. **Basic Statistical Analytics Only:** The Training Manager's statistics dashboard (UC-26) provides only fundamental, pre-built statistical visualizations, including: interview pass/fail rates, student distribution by major/enterprise, and grade distribution histograms. The system does not feature advanced analytics capabilities such as AI-driven predictive models, trend forecasting, natural language processing of report content, or custom query builders.  
- L7. **No Offline Functionality:** As a purely web-based platform, the UEIMS requires a continuous, active internet connection for all operations. Users cannot perform any system tasks (submitting reports, grading students, reviewing applications) while disconnected. There is no local data caching, offline mode, or background synchronization mechanism.  
- L8. **Single Language Interface:** The system's user interface, error messages, notification templates, and documentation are developed exclusively in English. Dynamic multi-language translation or localization for other languages (e.g., Vietnamese, Japanese) is not supported in the current version.

**3.3. Compatibility Limitations:**

- L9. **Modern Browser Requirement:** The system's UI/UX is designed, tested, and optimized exclusively for modern evergreen web browsers: Google Chrome (v90+), Microsoft Edge (v90+), Mozilla Firefox (v88+), and Apple Safari (v14+). Legacy browsers, most notably Internet Explorer 11 and older versions, are explicitly unsupported and may exhibit layout rendering errors or JavaScript incompatibilities.  
- L10. **Responsive Web Only (No Native Mobile App):** While the system's web interface is responsive and adapts to different screen sizes (desktop, tablet, mobile), it is not a native mobile application. Push notifications, biometric authentication, and other mobile-native features are not available.

## **4\. Exclusions**

- E1. **Financial, Payroll, & Compensation Management:** The system strictly manages the academic training lifecycle. It completely excludes any features related to tracking, calculating, or disbursing internship allowances, stipends, enterprise payroll, tax documentation, social insurance, or any form of financial compensation for the students or enterprises.  
- E2. **Legal Contract & Digital Signature Management:** The system excludes the drafting, storage, verification, or management of legal internship employment contracts, Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs), or any documents requiring legally binding digital signatures (e.g., DocuSign, Adobe Sign) between the Student and the Enterprise.  
- E3. **General-Purpose Job Board or Alumni Recruitment:** The platform is designed exclusively for the structured academic OJT semester. It will not function as a general-purpose post-graduation job recruitment portal, alumni career services platform, or freelance marketplace. Job postings are strictly limited to internship positions within the context of an active University semester.  
- E4. **AI-Powered Automated Screening or Grading:** While the system manages the end-to-end recruitment and grading workflows, it explicitly excludes the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), or Natural Language Processing (NLP) to: automatically screen or rank student CVs, auto-grade the textual content of weekly or final reports, or generate automated feedback.  
- E5. **Background Verification & Security Checks:** The system does not perform criminal record checks, financial credit checks, academic integrity investigations, or any form of deep background verification on students on behalf of Enterprises. Such verifications, if required, must be conducted independently by the Enterprise through their own HR processes.  
- E6. **Enterprise Internal HR & Operations Management:** The system's scope is strictly limited to the student's internship lifecycle within the university-enterprise partnership. It excludes features for managing the enterprise's internal HR workflows (employee attendance tracking, internal performance reviews, project management tools, or enterprise-level reporting unrelated to student interns).  
- E7. **Third-Party Single Sign-On (SSO) Integration:** Integration with external identity providers such as Google SSO, Microsoft Azure Active Directory, Facebook Login, or university-specific LDAP/CAS authentication systems is excluded from the current project phase. All authentication is handled internally (see Dependency D8).  
- E8. **Automated Notification Escalation & SLA Enforcement:** The system provides basic notification dispatching (email alerts, in-app notifications) but does not enforce Service Level Agreements (SLAs). For example, if an Enterprise fails to review a weekly report within 7 days, the system will not automatically escalate the issue, reassign the student, or impose penalties. Such escalations require manual intervention by the Training Manager.

## **5\. Business Rules**

*\[Provide common business rules that you must follow. The information can be provided in the table format as the sample below\]*

| ID | Name | Category | Rule Definition |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **BR-01** | Account Lockout | Constraints | User accounts are temporarily locked for 30 minutes after 5 consecutive failed login attempts. |
| **BR-02** | Simultaneous Session Control | Constraints | A user can only maintain one active session. Logging in from a new device invalidates the previous session. |
| **BR-03** | Token Expiration | Constraints | User session tokens automatically expire after 15 minutes of complete inactivity. |
| **BR-04** | Password Complexity | Constraints | Passwords must be at least 8 characters long, containing uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters. |
| **BR-05** | Unique Email Constraint | Constraints | The email address must be universally unique across all roles in the system. |
| **BR-06** | Single Role Assignment | Facts | An account can only possess one primary role (e.g., a student cannot simultaneously be an enterprise representative). |
| **BR-07** | Audit Log Append-Only | Constraints | System logs are immutable. They can only be appended to and never deleted or modified. |
| **BR-08** | Unique Semester Code | Constraints | Semester codes (e.g., SU26) must be strictly unique system-wide. |
| **BR-09** | Timeline Integrity | Constraints | A semester's Start Date must strictly precede its End Date. |
| **BR-10** | Initial Semester Status | Facts | Newly created semesters must inherently start with the "Draft" status. |
| **BR-11** | Locked Semester Edit Block | Constraints | Semesters holding a "Locked" status are read-only and cannot be edited. |
| **BR-12** | Date Modification Constraint | Constraints | Modifying dates of an "Active" semester is restricted and requires overriding confirmations. |
| **BR-13** | Status State Machine | Facts | Semester status only transitions forward: Draft → Open → Active → Closed → Locked. |
| **BR-14** | Permanent Lock Implication | Constraints | Setting status to "Locked" permanently freezes all related OJT data (Read-Only). |
| **BR-15** | Rejection Justification Mandatory | Constraints | Training Managers must provide written reasons when rejecting Enterprise accounts. |
| **BR-16** | TM Exclusive Access | Constraints | Only the Training Manager role is authorized to view the Eligible OJT Student list. |
| **BR-17** | Excel Mandatory Fields | Constraints | Excel imports require: Student ID (Unique), Full Name, Major, GPA, and Current Semester. |
| **BR-18** | Duplicate ID Handling | Constraints | New Excel imports overwrite existing student data ONLY IF current status is 'Eligible' or 'Pending'. |
| **BR-19** | Minimum Eligibility GPA | Constraints | Students must hold a GPA of 2.0 or higher to be imported into the Eligible list. |
| **BR-20** | Export Volume Limit | Constraints | Data exports are capped at a maximum of 10,000 records per transaction. |
| **BR-21** | Approval Data Lock | Constraints | Approving the Official OJT List automatically locks those students' placement records. |
| **BR-22** | Prerequisite Status Validation | Constraints | Official OJT approval is strictly limited to students with "Accepted" or "Matched" statuses. |
| **BR-23** | High-Privilege Action Logging | Constraints | Cancelling a student's OJT result requires deep audit logging (User ID, Reason, Timestamp). |
| **BR-24** | Admin Intervention Requirement | Constraints | Cancelling an already "OJT" status student requires System Administrator validation. |
| **BR-25** | Warning Eligibility | Constraints | Warning notifications can only be dispatched to students who missed the current active week's report. |
| **BR-26** | Incident Resolution Log | Constraints | Training Managers must document the specific resolution approach before closing an incident ticket. |
| **BR-27** | Grade Range | Constraints | Final course grades must be decimal values strictly between 0.0 and 10.0 inclusive, with up to one decimal place allowed. |
| **BR-28** | Feedback Confidentiality | Constraints | Student enterprise feedback is strictly internal. Only the Training Manager role can access feedback data. Enterprise accounts have no API or UI access to read this data. |
| **BR-29** | Post Ownership | Facts | Enterprises can exclusively manage (create/edit/close) their own job postings. |
| **BR-30** | Closed Post Block | Constraints | Setting a job post to "Closed" instantaneously blocks any new student applications. |
| **BR-31** | CV Format Rule | Constraints | All CVs must be strictly uploaded and processed in PDF format. |
| **BR-32** | CV Ownership Scope | Facts | Enterprises can only download CVs of students who applied directly to their active posts. |
| **BR-33** | Applicant Evaluation Lock | Constraints | An application moved to "Pass" or "Reject" cannot be reverted back to "Pending" by the enterprise. |
| **BR-34** | Interview Visibility Rules | Facts | Enterprises only see interview schedules linked to their own job posts. |
| **BR-35** | Interview Time Validation | Constraints | Scheduled interview times must be in the future and cannot overlap with existing appointments. |
| **BR-36** | Interview Eligibility Rule | Constraints | Only applicants who passed the CV screening phase are eligible for interview scheduling. |
| **BR-37** | Recruitment Result Rules | Constraints | Final recruitment results (Pass/Fail) can only be logged after the interview session concludes. |
| **BR-38** | Plan Mandatory Fields | Constraints | Enterprise must provide "Task Description" and "Target Date" for each training plan item. |
| **BR-39** | Plan Date Boundary Rule | Constraints | Internship plan dates must fall strictly within the official Start and End dates of the semester. |
| **BR-40** | Mandatory Feedback on Rejection | Constraints | Enterprise MUST provide written feedback when rejecting a student's weekly report. |
| **BR-41** | Incident Report Completeness | Constraints | Both "Incident Category" and "Incident Description" are mandatory to submit an incident report. |
| **BR-42** | Rubrics All Criteria Mandatory | Constraints | All 4 evaluation criteria must be scored before the enterprise can submit the final evaluation. |
| **BR-43** | Weighted Score Formula | Computations | Final Score \= (Attitude × 0.2) \+ (Professionalism × 0.4) \+ (Soft Skills × 0.2) \+ (Progress × 0.2). |
| **BR-44** | One-Time Evaluation Lock | Constraints | Once submitted, the enterprise's evaluation rubrics form is permanently locked. Modifications require a manual unlock request approved by the Training Manager. |
| **BR-45** | CV Size Limit | Constraints | CV files cannot exceed 5MB in storage size. |
| **BR-46** | Single Active Application | Constraints | A student can only have 1 active application submitted to a specific job post at any time. |
| **BR-47** | Application Snapshot | Facts | Student profiles are snapshotted at submission; future profile edits do not alter past applications. |
| **BR-48** | Withdrawal Deadline | Constraints | Students can only withdraw their CV before the job posting's defined deadline. |
| **BR-49** | Attendance Confirmation Irreversibility | Constraints | Once an interview attendance is confirmed by a student, they cannot cancel it via the UI. |
| **BR-50** | Final Report Format | Constraints | The final internship report must be strictly submitted in PDF format. |
| **BR-51** | Absolute Hard Deadline | Constraints | The server rejects any final report submissions received after the exact minute of the deadline. |
| **BR-52** | Grade Access Control | Facts | Internship evaluation scores are accessible only to the student owning the record, the Enterprise that submitted the evaluation, and the Training Manager for grading purposes. |
| **BR-53** | Single Feedback Per Semester | Constraints | A student can only submit one feedback entry per enterprise per semester. Duplicate submissions are blocked by the system. |
| **BR-54** | Semester-Based Student Permissions | Facts | Student access to system features is determined by their current\_semester value: Semester 1-4 can only browse job posts; Semester 5 can apply for jobs; Semester 6 can submit weekly reports and participate in active internship; Semester 7-9 can view historical results and submit enterprise feedback. |
| **BR-55** | Feedback Rating Scale | Constraints | Enterprise feedback scores must be integer values between 1 and 5 inclusive for each evaluation criterion (Training Quality, Supervisor Support, Work Environment, Overall). |
| **BR-56**  | Weekly Report Submission Window  | Constraints  | Students are only permitted to submit a weekly report during its designated "Active" week. Retroactive (past) and advance (future) submissions are strictly blocked. Late submissions are only accepted via explicit Training Manager override. |
